title: Lay the monorepo baseline: workspaces, manifests, tooling and agent configs
content:
Read `docs/build/README.md` first. Spec: `docs/specs/2026-10-25-powerbi-metrics-book.md`, sections Versions, Repository layout, Development workflow, Security ("What agents must do").

**What.** The skeleton every later issue builds in. No product code. Adapt from Metrics Book (`../metrics-book`, read only) wherever the same file exists there; keep its comments' style and its reasons.

1. **pnpm workspace.** Root `package.json` (`"private": true`, `packageManager: "pnpm@11.17.0"`, engines node `>=24 <25`), `.npmrc` (as Metrics Book's), `.node-version` (`24`), `pnpm-workspace.yaml` listing `apps/api`, `apps/web`, `apps/docs`, `packages/tokens`, `packages/powerbi-mock`, with Metrics Book's `allowBuilds` and any minimum-release-age setting it uses. Root scripts: `fmt` (`prettier --write .`), `fmt:check`, `lint` (`eslint .`), `typecheck` (`pnpm -r --if-present typecheck`), `test` (`pnpm -r --if-present test`).
2. **Every package's `package.json`, with every dependency v1 needs, pinned exact**, so later issues rarely touch a lockfile. Each must be at least a day old today; where a version below is younger, take the newest that is not and say so in your report.
   - root devDependencies: `@eslint/js@10.0.1`, `eslint@10.13.0`, `globals@17.13.0`, `lefthook@2.2.2`, `prettier@3.9.10`, `typescript@6.0.3`, `typescript-eslint@8.72.0`.
   - `apps/api` (`@powerbi-metrics-book/api`, `"type": "module"`): dependencies `hono@4.13.13`, `@hono/node-server@2.1.5`, `hono-openapi@1.5.0`, `zod@4.6.7`, `drizzle-orm@0.45.4`, `pg@8.23.1`, `better-auth@1.7.12`, `@better-auth/sso@1.7.12`, `@better-auth/passkey@1.7.12`, `@better-auth/oauth-provider@1.7.12`, `@cerbos/http@0.30.1`, `croner@10.0.1`, `age-encryption@0.3.1`, `yaml@2.9.1`; devDependencies `@types/node@24.19.2`, `@types/pg@8.23.1`, `drizzle-kit@0.31.11`, `tsx@4.23.15`, `vitest@5.0.5`, `@powerbi-metrics-book/powerbi-mock` (`workspace:*`). Scripts: `build` (`tsc -p tsconfig.build.json`), `test` (`vitest run`), `typecheck` (`tsc --noEmit`), `db:generate` (deletes `drizzle/` and runs `drizzle-kit generate`; see the README's Migrations).
   - `apps/web` (`@powerbi-metrics-book/web`): dependencies `react@19.3.1`, `react-dom@19.3.1`, `@tanstack/react-router@1.170.46`, `@tanstack/react-query@5.104.5`, `openapi-fetch@0.17.0`, `lucide-react@1.61.0`, `@enum-studio/tokens` (`workspace:*`); devDependencies `vite@8.3.5`, `@vitejs/plugin-react@6.1.2`, `tailwindcss@4.3.3`, `@tailwindcss/vite@4.3.3`, `openapi-typescript@7.13.0`, `@types/react@19.3.0`, `@types/react-dom@19.3.0`, `vitest@5.0.5`, `@playwright/test@1.64.1`, `typescript@6.0.3`. No scripts yet (the web issue adds them).
   - `apps/docs` (`@powerbi-metrics-book/docs`): dependencies `astro@7.4.2`, `@astrojs/starlight@0.42.7`, `@enum-studio/tokens` (`workspace:*`). No scripts yet.
   - `packages/tokens` (`@enum-studio/tokens`): dependencies `@fontsource-variable/inter@5.3.0`, `@fontsource/ibm-plex-mono@5.3.0`; devDependencies `vitest@5.0.5`. Script `test`.
   - `packages/powerbi-mock` (`@powerbi-metrics-book/powerbi-mock`, `"type": "module"`): dependencies `hono@4.13.13`, `@hono/node-server@2.1.5`, `jose@6.2.13`; devDependencies `@types/node@24.19.2`, `typescript@6.0.3`, `vitest@5.0.5`. Scripts `test`, `typecheck`, `build`.
   Run `pnpm install` and commit `pnpm-lock.yaml`.
3. **uv workspace.** Root `pyproject.toml` (as Metrics Book's: `requires-python = "==3.13.*"`, `[tool.uv] package = false`, workspace member `apps/cli`, dev group `pytest==9.1.1`, `mypy==2.4.0`, `types-PyYAML==6.0.12.20260906`), `.python-version` (`3.13`), `apps/cli/pyproject.toml` (distribution `powerbi-metrics-book` version 0.1.0, src layout, package `powerbi_metrics_book`, script `pbmb = "powerbi_metrics_book.cli:app"`, dependencies `typer==0.27.3`, `httpx==0.28.1`, `rich==15.0.0`, `pyyaml==6.0.3`, `ruff==0.17.2`), `apps/cli/src/powerbi_metrics_book/__init__.py` holding only `__version__ = "0.1.0"`, and `py.typed`. `cli.py` and `commands/` belong to the CLI issue: do not create them. Run `uv lock`, commit `uv.lock`.
4. **Shared configs**, adapted from Metrics Book's files of the same names: `tsconfig.base.json` (strict, the options Metrics Book's `apps/api/tsconfig.json` sets), `eslint.config.mjs` (typescript-eslint strict type-checked, ignoring `dist/`, `node_modules/`, generated files), `.prettierrc.json`, `.prettierignore` (add `pnpm-lock.yaml`, `apps/api/drizzle/`, `apps/api/openapi.json`, `.sudocode/`), `ruff.toml`, `mypy.ini` (strict).
5. **Per-package TypeScript and test configs**, so later issues can write code and tests at once: `apps/api/tsconfig.json`, `apps/api/tsconfig.build.json`, `apps/api/vitest.config.ts` (include `src/**/*.test.ts` and `src/**/*_security_test.ts`; no `globalSetup`: the api core issue adds it), `apps/api/drizzle.config.ts` (schema `./src/db/schema/index.ts`, out `./drizzle`, dialect `postgresql`), `packages/powerbi-mock/tsconfig.json`, `packages/powerbi-mock/vitest.config.ts`, `packages/tokens/vitest.config.ts`.
6. **lefthook.yml**: pre-commit jobs `pnpm exec prettier --check {staged_files}`, `pnpm exec eslint {staged_files}` (TypeScript only), `uv run ruff format --check` and `uv run ruff check` (Python only). Never installed automatically.
7. **`.gitignore`**: keep the line already there (`.sudocode/merge-driver.log`); add `node_modules/`, `dist/`, `.venv/`, `.env`, `.env.*` (not `.env.example`), `coverage/`, `playwright-report/`, `test-results/`, `.astro/`, `**/identity/`, `*.key`, `.DS_Store`.
8. **`.github/`**: `workflows/merge-gate.yml` on `pull_request` only: frozen `pnpm install`, `uv sync --locked`, `prettier --check`, `eslint`, `pnpm typecheck`, `ruff check`, `mypy apps/cli/src`, and the migration check (`pnpm --filter @powerbi-metrics-book/api db:generate` then `git diff --exit-code apps/api/drizzle`). Every action pinned by full commit SHA with the version in a comment, `permissions: contents: read`, a concurrency group, `timeout-minutes: 10`, no test jobs, no services (Martin's rule: the gate catches merge accidents, testing happens locally). `CODEOWNERS` (`@mbrummerstedt` on `apps/api/src/http/`, `apps/api/src/services/{auth,access,secrets,settings,connection}/`, `apps/api/src/mcp/`, `stack/`, `access/`, `.github/`, `docs/security/`), `pull_request_template.md` (adapt Metrics Book's: what changed in plain words, areas touched, the tier run with counts and duration, security review for sensitive paths; drop `expected_changes`, which is about warehouse numbers), `ISSUE_TEMPLATE/bug.md` and `ISSUE_TEMPLATE/feature.md`.
9. **Agent configs**, adapted from Metrics Book's: `.claude/settings.json` (allow `pnpm`, `uv`, `pbmb`, `docker compose` in this repository; deny reading `.env*`, `**/*.key`, `**/identity/**`), `.codex/config.toml`, `.codex/rules/default.rules`, `.cursor/environment.json`, `.cursor/mcp.json`, `.mcp.json` (the connector `powerbi_metrics_book` at `http://localhost:<port>/api/mcp`, with Metrics Book's comment about the port), `.devcontainer/devcontainer.json` (Node 24, Python 3.13, uv, pnpm, Docker in Docker).
10. **Scanner configs**: `.gitleaks.toml` (adapt), `.semgrep/rules/no_fetch_outside_guarded_fetcher.yml` (TypeScript under `apps/api/src/` except `apps/api/src/http/fetcher.ts`; adapt Metrics Book's rule and its test file `.semgrep/rules/no_fetch_outside_guarded_fetcher.ts`), `.semgrep/rules/no_sql_built_by_string_formatting.yml` with its `.ts` and `.py` test files (adapt).

title: Write the standards, the security docs, the AGENTS.md files and the licence files
content:
Read `docs/build/README.md` first. Spec: `docs/specs/2026-10-25-powerbi-metrics-book.md`, sections Security (all of it), Rules that will be load-bearing, Docs, skills and the open-source files ("Agent guidance and the open-source files"), The metrics book ("Conventions"), Development workflow. Writing rules: `~/.claude/docs/writing.md` (point first, plain words, no em or en dashes).

Adapt from Metrics Book (`../metrics-book`, read only), so the two read alike: `AGENTS.md`, `apps/*/AGENTS.md`, `docs/standards/{naming,typescript,python}.md`, `docs/security/{threat_model,agents}.md`, `LICENSE`, `NOTICE`, `SECURITY.md`, `CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md`. Keep what holds here word for word; change what this product does differently, and leave out dbt, dlt, DuckDB, anfra, warehouses, templates and the project format.

Write:

1. `AGENTS.md` (root): what this repository is, the layout (spec, Repository layout), the 17 load-bearing rules (spec, word for word), what agents must do (the five rules), "before you touch" (which standard to read for which work), where things go (a route or MCP tool: a thin adapter over `apps/api/src/services/`; a table: a Drizzle module in `apps/api/src/db/schema/`; a security test: beside the code, `*_security_test.ts`; a decision: `docs/decisions/<part>.md`), how to check (the test tiers), Git flow. Short; it points at the docs instead of repeating them.
2. Area files, each short: `apps/api/AGENTS.md`, `apps/web/AGENTS.md`, `apps/cli/AGENTS.md`, `apps/docs/AGENTS.md`, `packages/powerbi-mock/AGENTS.md` (the mock answers as Microsoft documents; a shape change cites the Microsoft page or the `microsoft/PowerBI-CSharp` swagger), `packages/tokens/AGENTS.md`, `skills/AGENTS.md`, `stack/AGENTS.md`.
3. `docs/standards/naming.md`: Metrics Book's, with a short opening that says this is the default convention a company may change (the `metrics_book` preset), and with the dimension and term parts written for Power BI columns instead of dbt marts. Metric names, qualifiers, labels, the description shape and "period comparisons are not metrics" stay word for word.
4. `docs/standards/typescript.md` and `docs/standards/python.md`: Metrics Book's, adapted (the API section names `createApp(deps)`, services, Drizzle modules and grants, the guarded fetcher; the CLI section names `pbmb`).
5. `docs/security/threat_model.md`: this product's assets, who is trusted, attackers, trust boundaries with a drawing (internet and api; api, Cerbos and Postgres; api and worker; the api's outbound requests to Microsoft, Power BI, Graph and the embedding provider; the worker's to the scanner API; secrets and identities at rest; the person's Power BI tokens; results; the setup link; the supply chain; the maintaining agent), the control holding each, the test proving each, residual risks, and when the model must be updated. Use the spec's Security section as the summary it expands.
6. `docs/security/agents.md`: Metrics Book's five rules with examples set in this product (a client secret entered through `pbmb admin secrets set`, never echoed; the scanner's secret readable only by the worker; results bound to their owner).
7. `LICENSE` (Apache-2.0, full text), `NOTICE` (Copyright 2026 Enum Studio ApS), `SECURITY.md` (private reports through GitHub security advisories, scope, how fast we answer, supported versions), `CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md` (Contributor Covenant 2.1, contact through GitHub).
8. `docs/decisions/README.md`: how a decision file is written (the decision, why, when it stops being right), as Metrics Book's `docs/decisions/` files are.

`README.md` and `CONTRIBUTING.md` are written in the docs phase, when there is something to set up; do not write them here.

title: Build the DAX module: tokeniser, normaliser, expansion, fingerprint, variant patterns
Build the CLI's core: the Typer app, the API client, credentials and output
content:
Read `docs/build/README.md` first ("CLI (package `powerbi_metrics_book`)"). Spec: `docs/specs/2026-10-25-powerbi-metrics-book.md`, section The CLI. Standard: Metrics Book's `docs/standards/python.md` (`../metrics-book/docs/standards/python.md`) until this repository's lands.

Adapt from Metrics Book's CLI (`../metrics-book/apps/cli/src/metrics_book/cli.py` and its command registration), so the two CLIs can later share a library.

Build in `apps/cli/src/powerbi_metrics_book/`:

1. `cli.py`: `app`, the Typer app behind `pbmb`, registering every module in `commands/` (a module with `app: typer.Typer` is a group, one with `command` a single command), with global options `--url` (else `PBMB_URL`, else the URL saved at login) and `--json`.
2. `client.py`: `Client`, every remote command's way to `/api/v1`: base URL, credentials in the spec's order (`PBMB_API_KEY` as `Authorization: Bearer`; else the saved device-flow token, refreshed once through the saved refresh token when the api answers 401, the new token saved), a 60-second timeout, JSON in and out, and the api's error shape `{ "error": kind, "message": ... }` turned into `ApiError(kind, message, status)`. No retries beyond the one refresh.
3. `credentials.py`: `~/.config/pbmb/credentials.json` (respecting `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`), written with mode 0600 inside a 0700 directory, refusing to read a file other users can read; holds the URL, access token, refresh token and expiry.
4. `output.py`: one helper every command uses: with `--json`, one JSON document on stdout and nothing else; without, a short human answer (tables with `rich`). Errors go to stderr as one sentence; exit codes `0` done, `1` failed, `2` usage, `3` not signed in, `4` refused or not found, `5` rate limited.
5. `commands/whoami.py`: `pbmb whoami` (`GET /api/v1/me`), the first command, which proves the chain end to end.

Tests (`apps/cli/tests/`, pytest) against `httpx.MockTransport`: credential order, the one refresh on 401, the credentials file's mode and refusal of a readable one, `--json` printing exactly one document, the exit codes per error kind.

title: Build the guarded fetcher, the only way the api reaches the network
content:
Read `docs/build/README.md` first (`GuardedFetcher` in "Interfaces fixed across tasks"). Spec: `docs/specs/2026-10-25-powerbi-metrics-book.md`, section Security ("Controls": Outbound requests). Threat model: Metrics Book's B6 (`../metrics-book/docs/security/threat_model.md`).

Implement `GuardedFetcher` (declared in `apps/api/src/context.ts`) in `apps/api/src/http/fetcher.ts`:

```ts
export function createGuardedFetcher(options: {
  allowedOrigins: () => Promise<string[]>;   // the fixed hosts, read from settings by the caller (Microsoft identity, Power BI, Graph, the embedding provider)
  nodeEnv: "development" | "test" | "production";
}): GuardedFetcher;
```

- `fetchUntrusted(url, init)`: `https` only; the host resolved once, every address refused when it is private, loopback, link-local, unique-local, carrier-grade NAT, multicast, unspecified or the cloud metadata address (`169.254.169.254`, `fd00:ec2::254`), and the connection made to the address that was checked (no second lookup, so DNS rebinding cannot swap it); 5 seconds in all; the body read up to 64 KiB and the request aborted past it; `redirect: "manual"`, and a 3xx answered as a refusal.
- `fetchFixed(url, init)`: the URL's origin must be one of `allowedOrigins()`; `https` only, except that when `nodeEnv` is `development` or `test` an `http` origin on a loopback address is allowed (the mock); `timeout_ms` defaults to 30,000 and may be raised to 300,000; `max_bytes` defaults to 16 MiB and may be raised to 32 MiB; no redirects.
- Each refusal is a `ServiceError("upstream", ...)` with a sentence naming what was refused and why, never the response body.
- Node's own `fetch` cannot pin the connection to a checked address; use `undici` (add it to `apps/api/package.json`, pinned, at least a day old) with a `connect.lookup` that checks and returns the address, or an equivalent you show in a test.

The semgrep rule from the baseline issue already refuses `fetch` elsewhere under `apps/api/src/`.

Tests: `fetcher.test.ts` (a fixed host in the list is reached; size and time limits; no redirect followed) and `fetcher_security_test.ts` (each refused range, a hostname that resolves to a private address through a stub lookup, a redirect, `http` to localhost refused when `nodeEnv` is `production`: the lock tested shut on its own, and a fixed-host call to a host outside the list).

files: apps/api/src/http/fetcher.ts, apps/api/src/http/fetcher.test.ts, apps/api/src/http/fetcher_security_test.ts, apps/api/package.json, pnpm-lock.yaml
depends: api_core
verify: export PATH=/opt/homebrew/opt/node@24/bin:$PATH && pnpm --filter @powerbi-metrics-book/api exec vitest run src/http/fetcher && pnpm --filter @powerbi-metrics-book/api typecheck
budget: 700 lines including tests
model: opus (a security boundary: server-side request forgery)
first test: `fetchUntrusted("https://metadata.test/")` where the stub lookup answers `169.254.169.254` is refused before any connection.

title: Build the api core: app, config, context, errors, gate, database and test harness
content:
Read `docs/build/README.md` first: its "Interfaces fixed across tasks" is this issue's contract, and every later issue builds on what you write. Spec: `docs/specs/2026-10-25-powerbi-metrics-book.md`, sections Architecture, Access ("Who the callers are"), Security ("Controls": HTTP, Database), Setup and the admin section ("Settings and secrets", the settings table).

Adapt from Metrics Book's `apps/api` (`../metrics-book/apps/api`, read only): `src/app.ts`, `src/config.ts`, `src/log.ts`, `src/version.ts`, `src/http/gate.ts`, `src/http/public-paths.ts` and its security test, `src/http/request-log.ts`, `src/db/migrate.ts`, `src/db/grants_security_test.ts`, `test/compose.yml`, `test/database.ts`, `test/global-setup.ts`. Keep their approach (one migration lock, per-checkout Postgres on a port from the checkout path's hash, tests that roll back what they write) unless this issue says otherwise.

Build:

1. `src/context.ts`: `Db`, `Container`, `AppDeps`, `ServiceContext` exactly as the README gives them, and the interfaces they name, declared here: `GuardedFetcher` (as in the README), `SettingsStore`, `SecretReader`, `SecretWriter`, `Access` (with `ResourceKind = "dataset" | "book" | "thread" | "query_log" | "result" | "admin"`). `SettingsStore` is typed by a `SettingValues` map declared here, one entry per setting: `powerbi.tenant_id`, `powerbi.app_client_id`, `powerbi.scanner_client_id` (string or null); `powerbi.authority`, `powerbi.api_url`, `powerbi.graph_url` (string); `powerbi.sync.schedule`, `powerbi.sync.full_scan_schedule` (string); `powerbi.sync.workspaces.include`, `powerbi.sync.workspaces.exclude` (string[]); `powerbi.sync.workspaces.personal`, `powerbi.service_account_queries`, `powerbi.connection_requires_matching_email` (boolean); `powerbi.keep_connections_alive_days` (number or null); `access.metadata_visibility` (`"powerbi" | "everyone" | "policy"`); `access.default_role` (string); `sign_in.providers` (array of `{ id: string; kind: "google" | "oidc"; label: string; client_id: string; issuer: string | null }`); `sign_in.passkeys` (boolean); `search.provider` (`"openai" | "gemini" | "none"`); `search.model`, `search.base_url` (string or null); `results.ttl_hours`, `results.preview_rows`, `results.page_rows_max`, `results.daily_row_budget`, `queries.rate_per_minute` (number); `setup.completed_steps` (string[]); `setup.completed_at` (string or null). `SettingKey = keyof SettingValues`.
2. `src/principal.ts` (the README's `Principal`), `src/errors.ts` (`ErrorKind`, `ServiceError`), `src/http/error-response.ts` (maps a `ServiceError` to the README's status codes and `{ error, message }`).
3. `src/config.ts`: `loadConfig(environment, container)` reads the bootstrap variables in the README's table (api: all of them; worker: no `MIGRATOR_DATABASE_URL`, `AUTH_SECRET`, `PORT`), failing at start with the variable's name. `ALLOW_DEV_SIGN_IN` is read as a boolean; `NODE_ENV` as `"development" | "test" | "production"`.
4. `src/log.ts`, `src/version.ts` as Metrics Book's.
5. `src/app.ts`: `createApp(deps: AppDeps): Hono<AppEnv>` with, in this order, the request log, security headers (`src/http/security-headers.ts`: CSP `default-src 'self'` with the exceptions the SPA needs later left out for now, `X-Frame-Options: DENY`, `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, `Referrer-Policy: same-origin`, HSTS when `PUBLIC_BASE_URL` is https, a 1 MiB body limit), the gate (`src/http/gate.ts`, `src/http/public-paths.ts`: Metrics Book's rule; public now: `/health`), the origin check (`src/http/origin-check.ts`: a POST, PUT, PATCH or DELETE must carry an `Origin` equal to `PUBLIC_BASE_URL`'s origin, except paths in an exported `ORIGIN_CHECK_EXEMPT` list, empty for now), `GET /health` (as Metrics Book's), `/api/v1` mounted from `src/routes/v1/index.ts` (`export function v1Routes(deps: AppDeps): Hono<AppEnv>`, holding no route yet; REST issues add theirs there), and an error handler that answers a `ServiceError` through `error-response.ts` and anything else as Metrics Book's does.
6. `src/db/client.ts` (`createPool(url)`, `createDb(pool)` with the schema), `src/db/migrate.ts` (Metrics Book's, then the grants, then every `src/db/sql/*.sql` file in name order; all idempotent), `src/db/grants.ts` (`declareGrants(...)`, as the README says; privileges may name columns, `"update(description, custom)"`; `applyGrants(client)` grants exactly what is declared and revokes what is not, for `api_rw`, `worker_rw` and `audit_writer`), `src/db/schema/index.ts` (no table yet), `src/db/grants_security_test.ts`.
7. `stack/postgres/init/01_roles_and_database.sh`: creates the database `powerbi_metrics_book`, the roles `migrator` (owner), `api_rw`, `worker_rw`, `audit_writer` with passwords from the container's environment, `create extension if not exists vector`, and revokes `public`'s rights (adapt Metrics Book's `stack/postgres/init/01_roles_and_databases.sh`, without its warehouse).
8. title: Build the mock's core: tenant model, Microsoft identity, Graph, embedding fakes, server
content:
Read `docs/build/README.md` first (the mock's routes are in "Names fixed across tasks"). Spec: `docs/specs/2026-10-25-powerbi-metrics-book.md`, sections Power BI ("Testing against Power BI", "A person's Power BI connection", "Workspaces and apps"), Access ("Sign-in and tokens"), Search ("The embedder").

`packages/powerbi-mock` answers as Microsoft, Graph, OpenAI and Gemini do, so the stack runs and is tested with no real tenant. This issue builds its core; the Power BI REST routes are the next issue, and the sample tenant the one after.

Build:

1. `src/tenant.ts`: the tenant model every route reads, as plain TypeScript types (no zod needed): `Tenant` with `tenant_id`, `people` (`object_id`, `email`, `user_principal_name`, `name`, `group_ids`, `revoked` flag), `groups` (`object_id`, `name`), `service_principals` (`app_id`, `object_id`, `secret`, `may_call_admin_apis` boolean), `apps_registrations` (client id, secret, redirect URIs, `kind: "confidential_web"`), `settings` (`detailed_metadata`, `dax_expressions`, `execute_queries`, `service_principals_admin_apis` booleans, all true by default), `workspaces` (id, name, type, state, `users: AccessEntry[]`, dataset ids, report ids), `apps` (id, name, description, workspace id, published by, last update, `users: AccessEntry[]`, report ids), `reports` (id, name, dataset id, app id or null), `datasets` (id, workspace id, name, description, configured by, storage mode, `has_row_level_security`, `schema_retrieval_error` or null, `tables` with columns, measures (name, expression, description, format string, hidden, display folder) and rows, `relationships`, `users: AccessEntry[]` for direct shares, `recorded_queries: { dax: string; rows: Record<string, unknown>[] }[]`). `AccessEntry` is `{ principal_type: "User" | "Group" | "App", object_id, email?, access_right }`. Export a small tenant for this package's own tests in `src/test-tenant.ts`.
2. `src/server.ts`: `createMockPowerBi(options: { tenant: Tenant; origin?: string })` returns a Hono app mounting the routes; `startMockPowerBi(options)` serves it on a free port and returns `{ url, close, setActingUser(object_id), failNext(route_prefix, status, retry_after_seconds?) }`; `src/index.ts` exports both and the types; `src/bin.ts` serves it on `PORT` with the sample tenant once that exists (until then the test tenant), for the dev compose file; `Dockerfile` for that.
3. **Microsoft identity** (`src/entra/**`), at `/{tenant}/oauth2/v2.0/authorize`, `/{tenant}/oauth2/v2.0/token` and `/{tenant}/discovery/v2.0/keys`:
   - an RS256 key pair made at start (`jose`), its JWKS served;
   - `authorize` (GET) checks `client_id`, `redirect_uri` against the registration, keeps the PKCE `code_challenge` (S256 only) and `scope`, and redirects with `code` and `state` for the acting person (`setActingUser`), or with `error=consent_required` when the person is `revoked`;
   - `token` (form POST) supports `client_credentials` (client id and secret checked; an app-only access token for `https://analysis.windows.net/powerbi/api/.default` naming the service principal's `oid` and `appid`), `authorization_code` (code once, verifier checked against the challenge, secret checked; answers `access_token` for the first non-OpenID resource in the scopes, `refresh_token`, `id_token`, `expires_in`, `scope`), and `refresh_token` (rotation: each use answers a new refresh token and the old one is spent; a spent or revoked one answers `invalid_grant`; the `scope` parameter picks the resource, so the same refresh token can be redeemed for Power BI or for Graph `User.Read`);
   - every JWT carries `iss = {origin}/{tenant}/v2.0`, `aud`, `tid`, `oid`, `exp`, `iat`; ID tokens add `email`, `preferred_username`, `name`, `nonce` when one was sent;
   - errors in Microsoft's shape (`error`, `error_description`, `error_codes`).
4. **A generic OpenID Connect provider** at `/oidc/` (discovery document, authorize, token, JWKS, userinfo), the stand-in for Okta or Keycloak when a test adds a second sign-in provider.
5. **Graph** at `/graph/v1.0/me/transitiveMemberOf`: with a Graph access token from the identity routes, the acting person's groups as directory objects (`@odata.type`, `id`), paged with `@odata.nextLink` at 2 per page so paging is tested.
6. **Embedding fakes**: `POST /openai/v1/embeddings` (Bearer key required, `model`, `input` string or array, `dimensions`) and `POST /gemini/v1beta/models/{model}:batchEmbedContents` (`x-goog-api-key` required, `requests[].content.parts[].text`, `outputDimensionality`). Vectors are deterministic per text (seeded from its SHA-256), unit length, of the asked dimension; usage reports a token count of words times 1.3 rounded up. A request with no key answers 401 in each provider's error shape.
7. Every route checks its bearer token's signature, audience and expiry, and answers 401 as Microsoft does when one fails.
8. **The build.** The baseline's `build` script emits tests and `vitest.config` into `dist/` and nests the output under `dist/src/`. Add `tsconfig.build.json` (only `src/`, tests excluded, `outDir: dist`, `rootDir: src`) and point `build` at it, so the Dockerfile copies `dist/` and runs `dist/bin.js`.
9. **A control route** (`src/control.ts`), so tests that drive the mock in its container (Playwright, the end-to-end test) can do what `startMockPowerBi`'s handle does in process: `POST /_mock/acting-user` (`{ object_id }`), `PATCH /_mock/settings` (any of the tenant `settings` booleans, and a service principal's `may_call_admin_apis`), `POST /_mock/fail-next` (`{ route_prefix, status, retry_after_seconds? }`), `POST /_mock/reset` (the tenant as it started). Mounted only when `createMockPowerBi` gets `control: true`; `bin.ts` passes it when `MOCK_CONTROL=1`. Tested: absent without the option, each action with it.

Tests (vitest, `src/**/*.test.ts`) for each route, including PKCE refusal on a wrong verifier, refresh token reuse refused, the refresh token redeemed for Graph, paging in Graph, and both embedding shapes.

title: Define the compose stack: containers, networks, hardening, Cerbos config, dev overlay
content:
Read `docs/build/README.md` first (compose services, networks, volumes, environment in "Names fixed across tasks"). Spec: `docs/specs/2026-10-25-powerbi-metrics-book.md`, sections Architecture, Security ("Controls": Network, Containers), Setup and the admin section ("Bootstrap values", identities), Development workflow.

Adapt from Metrics Book's `stack/compose.yml`, `stack/dev/compose.dev.yml`, `stack/cerbos/config.yaml` and its compose test (`../metrics-book`, read only; find the compose test with `grep -rl compose.yml --include='*test*' apps stack`).

Build:

1. `stack/compose.yml`: services `api` (image `powerbi-metrics-book`, built from `apps/api/Dockerfile` with context the repository root, command `api`; networks `edge`, `app`, `egress`; volume `api_identity` at `/var/lib/pbmb/identity`; the only published port, from `PBMB_PORT`, default 3000; depends on `postgres` healthy and `cerbos` healthy), `worker` (same image, command `worker`; networks `app`, `egress`; volume `worker_identity`), `postgres` (`pgvector/pgvector:pg18` pinned by digest; network `app`; volume `pgdata`; `stack/postgres/init/` mounted as init scripts; passwords for each role from the environment), `cerbos` (`ghcr.io/cerbos/cerbos:0.57.0` pinned by digest; network `app`; `stack/cerbos/config.yaml`; policies from `/policies`, which the image ships and a deployment's `access/policies` adds to). Every service: non-root user, `read_only: true` with `tmpfs` where it writes, `security_opt: [no-new-privileges:true]`, `cap_drop: [ALL]`, memory and CPU limits, a health check. Networks: `app` is `internal: true`; `edge` and `egress` are not. No service mounts the Docker socket; no volume is mounted by both `api` and `worker`. Find digests with `docker buildx imagetools inspect <image>`.
2. `stack/dev/compose.dev.yml`: adds `powerbi-mock` (built from `packages/powerbi-mock/Dockerfile`, on `egress` only (never `app`, where it could reach postgres and cerbos), with the alias the settings point at), sets `MOCK_CONTROL=1` on the mock (its test control route), `NODE_ENV=development`, `ALLOW_DEV_SIGN_IN=1`, and the settings environment overrides that point `powerbi.authority`, `powerbi.api_url`, `powerbi.graph_url` and `search.base_url` at the mock. Ports and the compose project name come from a hash of the checkout's path, as Metrics Book's dev overlay does.
3. `stack/cerbos/config.yaml`: disk storage at `/policies` with watching off, the audit log off (the api keeps the audit), schema enforcement as Metrics Book's.
4. `stack/env.example`: every bootstrap value, each with a comment saying what it is, and no real value.
5. `apps/api/src/stack/compose_security_test.ts`: reads `stack/compose.yml` (with the `yaml` package) and fails when a service other than `api` publishes a port, when `app` is not internal, when `api` and `worker` share a volume, when a service lacks any hardening key above, when an image other than `powerbi-metrics-book` is not pinned by digest, or when a service mounts the Docker socket.

`apps/api/Dockerfile` is the entries issue's; reference it, do not write it.

title: Build @enum-studio/tokens, the look both products share
content:
Read `docs/build/README.md` first. Spec: `docs/specs/2026-10-25-powerbi-metrics-book.md`, section The look ("One token set for both products"). Martin's design rules: `~/.claude/docs/design.md`.

The tokens implement Enum Studio's brand. Sources, read only:
- the brand: `git -C ../enumstudio show b702d1b6:docs/brand.md`;
- the light palette, type scale, spacing, radius and shell widths: `../enumstudio-metrics-book/src/styles/tokens.css` (the planner's; carry its comments' measured contrast ratios);
- the dark values: the admin's dark theme in `../enumstudio/src/styles/tokens.css` (green `#8fc1a6` on `#0b0d0f`; find its full dark set there, on `main` or on the branch `git log --all -- src/styles/tokens.css` names newest);
- the mark and the tile: `Mark.astro` and `public/favicon.svg` in the enumstudio repository (`git -C ... show <ref>:<path>`).

Build in `packages/tokens/`:

1. `tokens.css`: the planner's token names and light values on `:root`; a dark value for every colour token under `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)` guarded by `:root:not([data-theme="light"])`, and again under `:root[data-theme="dark"]`. One accent. No new token names beyond what both products need; where you add one, say why in a comment.
2. `theme.css`: a Tailwind 4 `@theme inline` block mapping the tokens to utilities (colours, the six type sizes, spacing, radius, fonts), so either product uses `bg-surface text-ink` and never a raw hex.
3. `fonts.css`: Inter (variable, optical sizing left to the browser) and IBM Plex Mono from the `@fontsource` packages, so no page loads a font from a third party.
4. `mark.svg` (the line mark, `currentColor`) and `tile.svg` (the favicon tile), copied as the brand file describes.
5. `contrast.test.ts`: parses `tokens.css` and checks every text-on-ground pair the planner's comments list, plus the same pairs in dark, at 4.5:1 or more; fails naming the pair and the ratio.
6. `README.md`: what the package is, how each product imports it (CSS entry points, the Tailwind theme, the favicon), and that a change to the look is one pull request here and one version bump in each product.
7. `package.json` `exports` for the CSS files and SVGs. `packages/tokens/AGENTS.md` is the standards issue's; do not write it.

title: Build the conventions: schema, both presets, the store and the checks that read them
content:
Read `docs/build/README.md` first. Spec: `docs/specs/2026-10-25-powerbi-metrics-book.md`, sections The metrics book ("Conventions: the company's rules, not ours" in full, "Metrics and variants", "Trust states"), Extending it. The default preset's guide is Metrics Book's naming standard: `../metrics-book/docs/standards/naming.md` (read only), adapted for Power BI as this repository's `docs/standards/naming.md` says once it exists.

Nothing about names, fields, variant axes, drafting or verification may be written into code: it is read from the conventions (load-bearing rule 11).

1. `apps/api/src/services/conventions/schema.ts`: a zod schema for the conventions document exactly as the spec's YAML shows it (every key, with `preset`), and `type Conventions`. A custom field is `{ key, label, type: "text" | "number" | "boolean" | "date" | "choice", values?, required }`; a custom axis `{ key, values }`.
2. `conventions/presets/metrics_book.yml` and `conventions/presets/minimal.yml` at the repository root: complete documents. `metrics_book` holds the spec's defaults and a guide (Markdown, self-contained, in plain words: the metric name kinds with examples, qualifier order, VAT, labels, the description shape with the spec's example, why a period comparison or a currency conversion is a variant, how terms work on columns). `minimal` asks only for a definition and a unit, sets `naming.case: none`, turns the naming checks off and keeps grouping by fingerprint.
3. `apps/api/src/services/conventions/store.ts`: `currentConventions(db)` (the newest version; on an empty table, the `metrics_book` preset, resolved), `setConventions(deps, principal, document)` (validates, resolves the preset with the overrides, stores a new version, records a `book_change` and a `conventions.changed` event in the same transaction), `diffConventions(current, proposed)` (a list of changed paths with before and after), `listVersions(db)`, `resolve(document)` (the preset merged under the document's own keys: objects merged deeply, arrays replaced).
4. `apps/api/src/services/book/checks.ts`: pure functions, no database:
   ```ts
   export type CheckableMetric = { name: string; label: string; name_is_generated: boolean; definition: string | null; aliases: string[] | null; when_to_use: string | null; not_the_same_as: string | null; grain_and_filters: string | null; unit: string | null; category_id: string | null; custom: Record<string, unknown> };
   export type CheckResult = { check: string; passed: boolean; message: string };
   export function checkMetric(metric: CheckableMetric, context: { conventions: Conventions; other_labels: string[]; live_base_variants: number }): CheckResult[];
   export function checkTerm(term: CheckableTerm, context: { conventions: Conventions; backed_by_columns: number }): CheckResult[];
   export function validateCustomFields(fields: CustomFieldSpec[], values: Record<string, unknown>): string[];   // problems, empty when valid
   ```
   One function per check in the spec's table, each named as the table names it, each reading its rule from `conventions` and skipped when `checks.off` lists it. A message is a sentence an agent can act on ("The key does not start or end with a kind the conventions name: number_of_, total_, ... Rename it.").

Tests: every check under `metrics_book` (passing and failing rows), the same metrics under `minimal`, a changed convention changing a result (a company that adds `_dkk` to `naming.kinds` sees it pass), custom fields required and of the right type, `resolve` merging, `setConventions` refusing an invalid document with the path of the problem, versions kept.

title: Build secrets: age identities per container, write-only storage, rotation
content:
Read `docs/build/README.md` first (`SecretReader`, `SecretWriter`, `SecretName`; bootstrap variables `API_AGE_IDENTITY`, `WORKER_AGE_IDENTITY`, `IDENTITY_DIR`). Spec: `docs/specs/2026-10-25-powerbi-metrics-book.md`, sections Setup and the admin section ("Settings and secrets": each secret encrypted to the containers that read it; the secrets table with who reads each), Security ("Secrets and tokens at rest", the checklist rows on secrets).

Implement, in `apps/api/src/services/secrets/`:

1. `age.ts`: the one module that imports `age-encryption` (0.3.1, pre-1.0, so it is wrapped here alone): `generateIdentity()`, `recipientOf(identity)`, `encryptFor(recipients: string[], text: string): Promise<Uint8Array>`, `decryptWith(identity: string, ciphertext: Uint8Array): Promise<string>`.
2. `identity.ts`: `loadIdentity(config: Config): Promise<{ identity: string; recipient: string }>`: the environment variable for this container when set; else the file `<IDENTITY_DIR>/<container>.key`, created with mode 0400 on first start (refusing to use a file other users can read); then publishes the recipient to `container_identity` (insert when new; the row of a replaced recipient gets `retired_at`).
3. `readers.ts`: which containers read which secret: `powerbi_scanner_client_secret` the worker; `powerbi_app_client_secret`, `result_link_key` and `sign_in_<provider>_client_secret` the api; `openai_api_key` and `gemini_api_key` both. A name outside it is refused.
4. `store.ts`: `createSecretReader(deps, identity)`: `read(name)` returns the environment variable of the same name upper-cased when set (only for a secret this container reads), else decrypts this container's ciphertext, else null; a secret this container does not read is refused with an error, never decrypted. `createSecretWriter(deps)` (api only): `write(name, value, by, expiresAt)` encrypts the value separately for each reader's current recipient (refusing when a reader has never published one: "the worker has not started yet"), stores the hint (last four characters), who, when and the expiry, and records an audit event when the audit writer exists (leave a clear seam: `onWrite` callback); `generate(name)` for `result_link_key` (32 random bytes, never shown); `list()` (name, readers, set or not, hint, set by, set at, expiry, check status): no value, ever.
5. `rotate.ts`: `rotateIdentity(deps)`: a new identity for this container, every secret it reads decrypted with the old and encrypted with the new, the old identity's row retired, the old key file kept as `<container>.key.retired-<timestamp>` until the run succeeds. Tokens of the Power BI connection join this later (that issue owns it).
6. `apps/api/src/server.ts`: the image's `server` command, `server rotate-identity` and a dispatcher later issues add to (`server setup-link` comes with the setup issue). It loads the config, the database and the identity, and runs one subcommand.
7. `apps/api/src/db/schema/secrets.ts`: `secret`, `secret_ciphertext`, `container_identity` as the spec gives them. Grants: `api_rw` select, insert, update and delete on `secret` and `secret_ciphertext`, select, insert and update on `container_identity`; `worker_rw` select on all three, insert and update on `container_identity`. A role can read the other container's ciphertext rows, which is harmless: only the matching identity decrypts them, and a test proves it.

Security tests, in these files because the spec's security checklist and the docs name them: `apps/api/src/services/secrets/secret_at_rest_security_test.ts` (a stored ciphertext never contains the value; a database dump alone decrypts nothing), `scanner_secret_isolation_security_test.ts` (the api's identity cannot decrypt `powerbi_scanner_client_secret`), `secret_write_only_security_test.ts` (no exported function returns a stored value to anyone but its reader), and beside them: a stored ciphertext never contains the value; the api's identity cannot decrypt `powerbi_scanner_client_secret`; no exported function returns a stored value to anyone but its reader; an identity file readable by others is refused; `rotateIdentity` leaves every secret readable with the new identity and none with the old.

title: Build access: the Cerbos client, the default policies and the describe filter
content:
Read `docs/build/README.md` first (`Access` in "Interfaces fixed across tasks"). Spec: `docs/specs/2026-10-25-powerbi-metrics-book.md`, sections Access ("Decisions (Cerbos)" in full, "Roles"), Power BI ("Workspaces and apps"), Extending it. Cerbos docs for policies, derived roles, policy tests and the `planResources` API: https://docs.cerbos.dev (read the pages for the version pinned, 0.57).

1. `access/policies/` at the repository root (built into the image later; a deployment adds its own): resource policies for `dataset`, `book`, `thread`, `query_log`, `result`, `admin`, and derived roles, implementing the spec's defaults:
   - `dataset:describe`: when `P.attr.metadata_visibility` is `everyone`, anyone signed in; when `powerbi`, when `R.attr.workspace_id` is in `P.attr.powerbi_workspace_ids`, or `R.attr.app_ids` intersects `P.attr.powerbi_app_ids`, or `R.id` is in `P.attr.powerbi_dataset_ids`; when `policy`, nothing in the defaults (the deployment's own policy decides). Service accounts: the same three lists, filled from what their admin gave them.
   - `dataset:query`: whoever may describe it, unless `R.attr.custom.queries_off` is true.
   - `book`: `curate` and `verify` for `curator` and `admin`; `approve` for them too (the browser-only rule is code, elsewhere); `edit_conventions` for `admin`.
   - `thread`: `create`, `reply`, `upvote` for anyone signed in; `accept` for the author or a curator; `archive` for a curator.
   - `query_log:read` for anyone signed in; `result:read` only when `R.attr.owner_id` is `P.id` (the code checks it too).
   - `admin`: every action for `admin`.
   Custom roles a deployment names in its own policies need no code.
2. `access/tests/`: Cerbos policy tests for every rule above, allowed and refused, each visibility mode, an app-only person, a person reaching through a group.

title: Build the Power BI, identity and Graph clients
content:
Read `docs/build/README.md` first. Spec: `docs/specs/2026-10-25-powerbi-metrics-book.md`, sections Power BI (all of it), Queries and results ("Running DAX" steps 5 and 6). Every request goes through `deps.fetcher.fetchFixed` (the guarded fetcher); base URLs come from the settings `powerbi.authority`, `powerbi.api_url` and `powerbi.graph_url`, so the tests point them at the mock.

Build in `apps/api/src/powerbi/`, each module a set of plain functions taking `AppDeps` (or the parts they need):

1. `identity.ts`: `scannerToken(deps)` (client credentials for the scanner registration, secret from `deps.secrets.read("powerbi_scanner_client_secret")`, scope `https://analysis.windows.net/powerbi/api/.default`, cached in memory until five minutes before expiry); `appServicePrincipalToken(deps)` (the same for the app registration, for service-account queries); `authorizationUrl(deps, { state, code_challenge, login_hint, scopes })`; `redeemCode(deps, { code, code_verifier, redirect_uri })` returning access token, expiry, refresh token, and `tid`, `oid`, `email`, `preferred_username` read from the ID token in the answer; `refresh(deps, refresh_token, resource: "powerbi" | "graph")` returning the new pair. Errors: `invalid_grant`, `invalid_client` and `unauthorized_client` become `ServiceError("needs_connection", ...)`; others `upstream`.
2. `scanner.ts`: `modifiedWorkspaces(deps, { since: Date | null })`, `startScan(deps, workspaceIds)` (at most 100), `waitForScan(deps, scanId, { poll_ms, timeout_ms })` (30-second polls by default, 30 minutes at most, a 429 waits its `Retry-After`), `scanResult(deps, scanId)` returning the typed result (`ScanResult`, written from the mock's and Microsoft's shape) with mashup expressions already removed (`source`, dataset `expressions`): the sync never sees them.
3. `admin.ts`: `listApps(deps)` (paged), `appUsers(deps, appId)`, `listReports(deps)` (paged; for apps the scan did not cover).
4. `execute.ts`: `executeQuery(deps, { token, dataset_id, dax, timeout_ms })` on the org path (`datasets/{id}/executeQueries`, never `groups/`), returning `{ columns: { name, type }[], rows: unknown[][], truncated: false } | { ..., truncated: true, note }`, with types inferred from the values, the 200-with-error answer turned into `truncated`, a DAX error (400) into `ServiceError("invalid", <Power BI's sentence>)`, 401/403/404 into `ServiceError("not_found", ...)`, 429 into `rate_limited` with the wait.
5. `graph.ts`: `myGroupIds(deps, graphToken)` following `@odata.nextLink`, returning group object ids only.
6. `errors.ts`: one place that reads Power BI's and Microsoft's error shapes into sentences.

Tests against the mock (`startMockPowerBi` with the mock's own test tenant): each function's success; scanner polling through `Running`; a 429 then success; an app-only person's query succeeding; a refresh token spent twice turning into `needs_connection`; mashup never present in `scanResult`'s answer.

title: Add the mock's Power BI REST routes: scanner, apps, reports, executeQueries
content:
Read `docs/build/README.md` first (the mock's routes). Spec: `docs/specs/2026-10-25-powerbi-metrics-book.md`, sections Power BI (all of it: the limits, the scanner flow, "Workspaces and apps", "Relationships and display folders", "Testing against Power BI"), Queries and results ("Running DAX" steps 5 and 6). Microsoft's shapes: the swagger at `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/microsoft/PowerBI-CSharp/master/sdk/swaggers/swagger.json` and the Microsoft Learn pages named in the spec; match field names and casing exactly (Power BI answers camelCase; keep it, it is Microsoft's wire, not ours).

Under `{origin}/powerbi/v1.0/myorg/`, reading the `Tenant` from `src/tenant.ts`:

1. **Scanner** (service principal tokens only; a principal whose `may_call_admin_apis` is false, or `settings.service_principals_admin_apis` false, answers 401 with Power BI's "API is not accessible for application" error): `GET admin/workspaces/modified` (`modifiedSince` validated between 30 minutes and 30 days old; `excludePersonalWorkspaces`, `excludeInActiveWorkspaces`), `POST admin/workspaces/getInfo` (1 to 100 ids; the query flags honoured: no `datasetSchema` means no tables; `settings.detailed_metadata` false means tables without columns and measures; `settings.dax_expressions` false means measures without `expression`; `getArtifactUsers` adds `users` to workspaces and datasets; reports carry `appId` and `datasetId`; a dataset's `schema_retrieval_error` is returned as `schemaRetrievalError` without tables), `GET admin/workspaces/scanStatus/{id}` (`Running` on the first poll, then `Succeeded`), `GET admin/workspaces/scanResult/{id}` (gone after 24 hours of mock time). Also the mashup the real API returns with the DAX setting: a table `source[].expression` and dataset `expressions`, so the sync's job of dropping them is tested.
2. **Apps and reports** (service principal): `GET admin/apps?$top=&$skip=`, `GET admin/apps/{appId}/users`, `GET admin/reports?$top=&$skip=`.
3. **executeQueries**, `POST datasets/{id}/executeQueries` and `POST groups/{groupId}/datasets/{id}/executeQueries`, with a person's delegated token or a service principal's:
   - who may query: a person reaching the dataset as a workspace member (directly or through a group), through an app audience, or by a direct share, with `settings.execute_queries` on; a service principal only as a workspace member, and never on a dataset with `has_row_level_security`; the `groups/` path also requires workspace membership, so an app-only person is refused there, as Microsoft's page says;
   - the engine: `EVALUATE '<table>'` and `EVALUATE TOPN(<n>, '<table>')` from the dataset's rows; `EVALUATE INFO.VIEW.RELATIONSHIPS()` and `EVALUATE INFO.VIEW.MEASURES()` from its model, in Power BI's column names (refused on a dataset whose fixture says so, as some tenants do); a `recorded_queries` match (whitespace-insensitive); anything else answers 400 in Power BI's DAX error shape;
   - the answer shape `{ results: [{ tables: [{ rows: [...] }] }] }` with row keys as Power BI writes them (`Table[Column]`, `[Measure]`), nulls when `includeNulls`; past 100,000 rows or 1,000,000 values the first rows and an `error` object beside them, with status 200, as Microsoft documents;
   - 120 requests a minute per identity, then 429 with `Retry-After`.
4. Every route honours `failNext` from the core, so a client's handling of 429 and 5xx is testable.

Tests per route, including: the app-only person queries through the org path and is refused on the `groups/` path; a service principal on a row-level-security dataset is refused; `getInfo` without the DAX setting has no expressions; the over-limit answer is partial with status 200.

title: Design the sample tenant and write down what the drafter and visibility must find in it
content:
Read `docs/build/README.md` first (the sample tenant's id; the clean-room rule: every name invented, starting from "Sample data"). Spec: `docs/specs/2026-10-25-powerbi-metrics-book.md`, sections Power BI ("Testing against Power BI": what the sample tenant must contain; "Workspaces and apps": the four access cases), The metrics book ("Drafts: how the sync groups measures", "Conventions": the `metrics_book` preset's drafting rules), Queries and results.

The sample tenant is the stack's test bed and its demo: the end-to-end test, the evals and `pnpm dev:up` all run on it. Its measures are written the way real Power BI models are, messy on purpose, so curation has real work in it. Build in `packages/powerbi-mock/src/sample/`:

1. `tenant.ts`: `sampleTenant(): Tenant` (the type from `src/tenant.ts`), deterministic. At least:
   - people (no stock names: role names like "Sample Admin" with `@sample.example` addresses): an admin, an analyst who is a member of the Sales workspace through the group "Sample data: Analysts", a viewer who reaches the Sales dataset only through the app "Sample data: Sales app", a person in the "Sample data: Leadership" group which is the audience of "Sample data: Leadership app" (Finance), and an outsider with no access; one person `revoked`, for the reconnect path;
   - service principals: the scanner (allowed admin APIs) and the app (a member of the Marketing workspace only, for service-account queries);
   - workspaces "Sample data: Sales", "Sample data: Finance", "Sample data: Marketing", and one personal workspace; datasets "Sample data: Sales", "Sample data: Finance", "Sample data: Marketing", one with row-level security, one with a `schema_retrieval_error`;
   - tables (Sales, Product, Customer, Date, Channel, Ad spend, Web sessions as fits each dataset), columns of every column type, relationships, display folders, a hidden helper measure, and generated rows (a few thousand sales rows, so a result pages and a CSV has weight);
   - measures that exercise every drafter rule: one calculation under two names in two datasets (grouped), the same one formatted differently with a comment (grouped), the same result written another way (`DISTINCTCOUNT` against `COUNTROWS(DISTINCT())`: not grouped), each period and comparison pattern of the DAX module once, a near miss of a pattern (an extra filter: not a variant), a measure reading `SELECTEDVALUE` of a currency slicer, a currency-converted measure through a rate table (not grouped, but named so `pbmb drafts next` suggests it), a title-string helper whose name starts with `_` (dismissed by the default conventions), a three-measure reference cycle;
   - recorded queries with their answers for the questions the end-to-end test and the evals ask (net sales by month last year; orders by channel).
2. `expected.ts`: what tests assert against, written by hand, not computed from the drafter: `EXPECTED_DRAFTS` (each expected metric group: its member measures by dataset and name, and each expected variant with its shift), `EXPECTED_NOT_GROUPED` (pairs that must stay apart, with why), `EXPECTED_DISMISSED`, `EXPECTED_CYCLE`, `EXPECTED_VISIBILITY` (per person, the datasets they may describe under `metadata_visibility: powerbi`), `EXPECTED_QUERY_ACCESS` (per person and dataset, org path and groups path).
3. `README.md`: the people, groups, workspaces, apps and datasets, and why each odd measure is there, in a table, so a test writer and an eval writer can find a case without reading the code. Say plainly that every name is invented sample data.
4. Make `src/bin.ts` serve the sample tenant.

Tests (`src/sample/sample.test.ts`): the tenant is deterministic (two calls give equal JSON); every measure, person and dataset that `EXPECTED_*` names exists in the tenant. (Whether the mock's routes answer as `EXPECTED_QUERY_ACCESS` says is tested later, with the routes and the sync.)

title: Build the settings store: registry, validation, environment overrides
content:
Read `docs/build/README.md` first ("settings and env overrides", `SettingsStore`). Spec: `docs/specs/2026-10-25-powerbi-metrics-book.md`, section Setup and the admin section ("Settings and secrets", the settings table with defaults).

Implement `SettingsStore` (declared in `apps/api/src/context.ts`, typed by its `SettingValues`):

1. `apps/api/src/services/settings/registry.ts`: `SETTINGS`, one entry per key of `SettingValues`, each with a zod schema, its default (the spec's table; `powerbi.authority` `https://login.microsoftonline.com`, `powerbi.api_url` `https://api.powerbi.com`, `powerbi.graph_url` `https://graph.microsoft.com`, `search.provider` `none`, `access.metadata_visibility` `powerbi`, `access.default_role` `viewer`, `sign_in.providers` `[]`, `sign_in.passkeys` `true`, `results.*` and `queries.rate_per_minute` as the spec says, the rest null, false or empty) and a one-sentence description the admin section and `pbmb admin settings` show. A test fails when a key of `SettingValues` has no entry.
Two values the api core left to this issue, decided by the coordinator: `powerbi.sync.workspaces.include` is `"all" | string[]` (workspace ids), default `"all"`; an empty list means no workspace is synced, never all of them. Change its type in `apps/api/src/context.ts` (`SettingValues`) to match; that one line is yours. `sign_in.passkeys` defaults to `false`.
2. `apps/api/src/services/settings/env.ts`: the environment variable for a key (README rule: `powerbi.sync.workspaces.include` is `POWERBI_SYNC_WORKSPACES_INCLUDE`), parsed as JSON for arrays and objects and coerced for scalars, validated by the same schema; a malformed value fails naming the variable.
3. `apps/api/src/services/settings/store.ts`: `createSettingsStore(db, environment)`: `get` (environment, then the database, then the default), `set` (validates, refuses a key the environment sets with `ServiceError("conflict", "... is set by the environment ...")`, records who and when), `source`, and `list()` (every key with its value, source and description, for the admin section).
4. `apps/api/src/db/schema/settings.ts`: `setting(key text primary key, value jsonb not null, set_by text not null, set_at timestamptz not null default now())`, a CHECK that `key` is one of the registry's keys (the database is the authority), grants: `api_rw` select, insert, update; `worker_rw` select. Add its export line to `schema/index.ts` and regenerate the migration.

Tests against real Postgres: defaults, an environment override winning and refusing `set`, validation refusing a bad value with the key named, the CHECK refusing an unknown key.

content:

Spec: `docs/specs/2026-10-25-powerbi-metrics-book.md`, sections The metrics book ("Data model": the mirror part), Power BI ("Workspaces and apps": `powerbi_access`, `person_identity`; "The sync": `sync_run`; "Relationships and display folders").

`apps/api/src/db/schema/mirror.ts`, Drizzle, exactly the columns the spec lists, plus:

- every mirror table (`powerbi_workspace`, `powerbi_app`, `powerbi_dataset`, `powerbi_table`, `powerbi_column`, `powerbi_measure`, `powerbi_relationship`) has `description text`, `described_by text`, `described_at timestamptz` and `custom jsonb not null default '{}'` (CHECK `jsonb_typeof(custom) = 'object'`);

title: Build the job queue, the runner, the schedule and the audit writer
content:
Read `docs/build/README.md` first (Jobs in "Interfaces fixed across tasks"). Spec: `docs/specs/2026-10-25-powerbi-metrics-book.md`, sections Architecture ("The units": worker, `job_request`, runner `api` and `worker`), Access ("Audit"), Security ("Database": `audit_writer`). Adapt the queue and advisory-lock approach from Metrics Book's spec ("How it grows", "Scheduling") and its runner (`../metrics-book/stack/runner/`, if it exists on its branch; read only).

Build:

1. `apps/api/src/db/schema/jobs.ts`: `job_request` as the spec gives it (CHECKs on `job`, `runner`, `trigger`, `status`); grants: `api_rw` select, insert, update; `worker_rw` select, insert, update.
2. `apps/api/src/services/jobs/queue.ts`: `enqueue(db, job)` (README signature); `take(db, runner)` takes the oldest queued job for this runner with `for update skip locked` and marks it running; `finish(db, id, outcome)`.
3. `apps/api/src/services/jobs/registry.ts`: `registerJob(name, runner, handler)` and `handlerFor(name)`.
4. `apps/api/src/services/jobs/runner.ts`: `runJobs(deps, { signal })`: a loop for `deps.container` that takes a job, holds a Postgres advisory lock for its job name while it runs (so two of one kind never overlap, even across replicas), marks it `skipped` when the lock is held elsewhere for longer than the job's `max_wait` (sync: 10 minutes), records `succeeded` or `failed` with the error's message, never its stack, and waits a second when the queue is empty. Stops cleanly on the signal.
5. `apps/api/src/services/jobs/schedule.ts`: `startSchedule(deps, entries)` with `croner`: each entry (`job`, a cron line or a function that reads one from settings, runner) enqueues a `job_request` with trigger `schedule` when it fires; a cron line that does not parse fails at start naming the setting.
6. `apps/api/src/db/schema/audit.ts`: `audit_event` as the spec gives it; grants: `audit_writer` insert only; `api_rw` and `worker_rw` select (the admin section reads it).
7. `apps/api/src/services/audit/write.ts`: `writeAudit(deps, event)` through `deps.auditDb`; `apps/api/src/services/audit/read.ts`: `readAudit(db, { since, principal, action, limit, before_id })`.

Tests against real Postgres: two runners never take one job; a second job of a held kind waits and is skipped after `max_wait`; a failed handler records `failed` and the loop goes on; a schedule fires an enqueue; `audit_writer` can insert into `audit_event` and cannot update or delete it (`audit_append_only_security_test.ts`).

title: Build the drafter: measures into draft metrics and variants, under the conventions
content:
Read `docs/build/README.md` first. Spec: `docs/specs/2026-10-25-powerbi-metrics-book.md`, sections The metrics book ("Metrics and variants", "Drafts: how the sync groups measures" in full, "Conventions": `drafting`, "Data model": `touched_at`, `assigned_by`, `origin`, `name_is_generated`, `dismissed_at`).

Consumes: the DAX module (`apps/api/src/dax/index.ts`: `expandMeasures`, `fingerprint`, `recogniseVariant`, `readsSelection`, `normalize`), the conventions (`currentConventions`, `Conventions`), `recordBookChange` and `withEvents` (README, "Book changes and events": each dataset's drafting runs in one `withEvents` transaction, emitting its `draft.created` and `variant.moved` events through `emit`; `recordBookChange` takes a `null` principal for the system).

Build `apps/api/src/services/book/drafter.ts`:

```ts
export function draftDatasets(deps: AppDeps, datasetIds: string[]): Promise<{ created: number; filed: number; regrouped: number; dismissed: number; deleted: number }>;
```

run by the worker after each sync, in one transaction per dataset, as the spec's steps say:

1. Update each live measure's `normalized_expression`, `fingerprint` (or `fingerprint_error` for a cycle) with the measures of its own dataset.
2. Skip what the conventions' `drafting.skip` names (hidden measures when set, display folders, tables, name patterns). Dismiss what `drafting.dismiss` names, with its reason, on a draft the sync owns.
3. Recognise variants (`recogniseVariant`) when `drafting.recognise_time_intelligence` is on; file the measure under its base's metric with the shift. Set `reads_selection` and `selection_columns`.
4. Group the rest by fingerprint across every dataset when `drafting.group_by_fingerprint` is on: an existing metric that holds a base variant with that fingerprint takes it; otherwise a new draft (`origin = 'sync'`, `trust_state = 'draft'`, `name_is_generated = true`, name from the most common measure name in snake_case, made unique with `_2`, `_3`; label from that measure name).
5. Only measures with no metric, or filed by the sync (`assigned_by = 'sync'`) under a metric whose `touched_at` is null, may be filed or moved. A curator's filing is never moved. A measure dismissed with an unchanged expression is not drafted again.
6. A draft the sync made, never touched, with no live variant left, is deleted.
7. Every metric created, variant filed or moved, draft dismissed or deleted gets a `book_change` (principal null means the sync; record it as `principal_kind = 'system'`, `principal_id = 'sync'`) and an event (`draft.created`, `variant.moved`).

Also `apps/api/src/services/book/suggestions.ts`: `suggestMerges(db, metricIds, conventions)`: drafts whose measure names differ only by a word in `drafting.name_hints` (period or currency), as likely merges with the word that differs; used by `pbmb drafts next` later.

Tests against real Postgres, with the sample tenant's datasets written into the mirror tables by a test helper (`apps/api/test/sample-mirror.ts`, which later issues reuse): the drafts equal `EXPECTED_DRAFTS`, the pairs in `EXPECTED_NOT_GROUPED` stay apart, `EXPECTED_DISMISSED` is dismissed, the cycle is recorded; a second run changes nothing; a curator's filing (set by the test) survives a run; a measure's expression changed under an untouched draft regroups it; under the `minimal` preset with `recognise_time_intelligence: false` no variant is recognised; `suggestMerges` offers the currency pair.

title: Build the sync job: scan, store the mirror, apps and access lists, then draft
content:
Read `docs/build/README.md` first. Spec: `docs/specs/2026-10-25-powerbi-metrics-book.md`, sections Power BI ("The sync" steps 1 to 8, "Workspaces and apps", "Relationships and display folders" item 1), The metrics book ("Drafts").

Consumes: `src/powerbi/{identity,scanner,admin}.ts` (the clients), `src/services/jobs/{registry,queue}.ts` (`registerJob`), `src/services/book/drafter.ts` (`draftDatasets`), the `sync_run` and mirror tables, the settings `powerbi.sync.*`, `withEvents` (README, "Book changes and events") for `sync.finished` and `sync.failed`.

Build `apps/api/src/services/sync/`:

1. `run.ts`: `runSync(deps, { kind: "incremental" | "full", trigger })`, registered as the worker's `sync` job (`registerJob("sync", "worker", ...)`, reading the job's `args: { kind: "incremental" | "full" }`, which the worker's deploy job and its schedule enqueue; add the module's import to `services/jobs/all.ts`), recording a `sync_run`. Incremental: `modifiedSince` = the start of the last successful sync; younger than 30 minutes: `skipped`; older than 30 days or none: a full sync. Full: every workspace. Filter by `powerbi.sync.workspaces.include`, `exclude` (names or ids) and `personal`.
2. Batches of 100 to `startScan`, at most four in flight, `waitForScan`, `scanResult`.
3. `store.ts`: for each scanned workspace, one transaction: upsert the workspace, datasets, tables, columns, measures and relationships (when the result carries `relationships`, with `relationships_source = 'scanner'`) in bulk statements, one per table kind, never one per row; set `removed_at` on items missing from a scanned workspace; clear `removed_at` on items that came back; keep a dataset's schema and record `schema_error` when it has `schemaRetrievalError` or `schemaMayNotBeUpToDate`; set `schema_changed_at` when anything in the dataset's schema changed and `expression_changed_at` on a measure whose expression changed. A measure missing in this sync while a new one with the same fingerprint (computed with the DAX module) appeared in the same dataset is a rename: update the row's name, keep its id and its variant. A workspace whose batch failed is not touched. A workspace whose state is deleted, or (full sync) no longer listed, is removed with everything in it.
4. `apps.ts`: on every sync, `listApps`; the datasets behind each app from the scan's reports (`appId`, `datasetId`), and on a full sync `listReports` for apps the scan did not cover; `powerbi_app` and `powerbi_app_dataset` replaced in one transaction.
5. `access-lists.ts`: `powerbi_access` from the scan's workspace and dataset `users` and, on a full sync, `appUsers` for every app; replaced per object in the same transaction as the object.
6. After storing: `draftDatasets` for every dataset whose schema changed, and an `embed` job enqueued (the search issue registers its handler; until then nothing takes it, which is fine: a queued job waits).
7. Events: `sync.finished` with counts, or `sync.failed` with the sentence.
8. Never store mashup: the client already drops it; a test proves no `source` expression and no dataset parameter reaches the database.

Tests against real Postgres and the mock with the sample tenant: a full sync stores what the sample tenant holds; a second sync with nothing changed writes no row (compare `synced_at` aside); a measure removed in the mock gets `removed_at` and its untouched draft is deleted; a renamed measure keeps its variant; a dataset with a schema error keeps its tables; a failed batch (`failNext` on `getInfo`) leaves its workspaces untouched; the app-only dataset is in `powerbi_app_dataset`; access lists match the tenant; the drafter's expected drafts exist after the sync; incremental within 30 minutes is skipped.

title: Build sign-in: Better Auth with Microsoft, other providers, passkeys, dev sign-in, roles, the person principal
content:
Read `docs/build/README.md` first (`Principal`, HTTP prefixes). Spec: `docs/specs/2026-10-25-powerbi-metrics-book.md`, sections Access ("Sign-in and tokens (Better Auth)" in full, "Roles"), Setup and the admin section (sign-in providers step, `access.default_role`), Security (the checklist row on sign-in; dev sign-in lock). Better Auth 1.7.12's Microsoft Entra ID provider source: https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/blob/v1.7.12/packages/core/src/social-providers/microsoft-entra-id.ts (options `tenantId`, `authority`, `disableDefaultScope`, `scope`, `disableProfilePhoto`, `mapProfileToUser`). Read the SSO and passkey plugins' docs for 1.7.12 before using them.

Build `apps/api/src/services/auth/`:

1. `better-auth.ts`: `createAuth(deps)`: Better Auth with the Drizzle adapter on the api's database (its tables in `apps/api/src/db/schema/auth.ts`, generated with Better Auth's CLI and committed; grants: `api_rw` only), `AUTH_SECRET`, `PUBLIC_BASE_URL`, secure cookies:
   - Microsoft: `tenantId` from `powerbi.tenant_id`, `authority` from `powerbi.authority` (the tests sign in against the mock), `clientId` from `powerbi.app_client_id`, the secret from `deps.secrets.read("powerbi_app_client_secret")`, `disableDefaultScope: true` with `openid profile email`, `disableProfilePhoto: true`; the ID token's `oid`, `tid` and, when present, `groups` captured into `person_identity` (when the token says groups overflowed, the connection reads them later);
   - the providers in `sign_in.providers`: `google` through Better Auth's Google provider, `oidc` through the SSO plugin with the provider's `issuer` (its discovery fetched through `deps.fetcher.fetchUntrusted`); their secrets from `sign_in_<id>_client_secret`; `groups` claims captured when present;
   - passkeys (the passkey plugin) when `sign_in.passkeys` is on, for people already signed in;
   - settings change rarely and Better Auth is configured at construction, so `createAuth` is cached by a hash of the settings and secrets it reads, and rebuilt when they change.
   Mount it on `/api/auth/*` in `app.ts`, and add its callback paths to the public-paths list with a test.
2. `dev-sign-in.ts`: `POST /api/auth/dev/sign-in` with an email, only when `NODE_ENV` is `development` or `test` and `ALLOW_DEV_SIGN_IN=1`; refused otherwise, each lock tested shut on its own (`dev_sign_in_security_test.ts`).
3. `roles.ts`: `role_assignment` (schema in `apps/api/src/db/schema/roles.ts`, as the spec gives it, grants `api_rw`), `resolveRoles(db, { email, group_ids, tenant_member })` (person, email domain, group, everyone in the tenant, plus `access.default_role` unless it is `none`), `assignRole`, `revokeRole`, `listAssignments`. At the sign-in callback, a person no assignment reaches is refused before an account is made (a Better Auth hook), with a sentence on the sign-in page.
4. `principal.ts`: `personPrincipal(deps, session)`: builds the `Principal` per request (`kind: "person"`, roles resolved now, never cached in the session, `via: "browser"`), and a Hono middleware `authenticate` that sets `c.var.principal` from a session cookie, leaving bearer tokens to the next issues (they add their branches here).
5. `apps/api/src/routes/v1/me.ts`: `GET /api/v1/me` (who, roles, sign-in method, the Power BI connection's state once that exists: until then `"not_connected"`), registered in `routes/v1/index.ts`.

Tests against real Postgres and the mock's identity and OIDC routes, the provider cases in `apps/api/src/services/auth/sign-in-providers.test.ts` (the spec's security checklist names it): Microsoft sign-in end to end through the mock (authorize, callback, session, `/api/v1/me`); a second provider through the mock's `/oidc`; a person with no assignment refused at the callback when `access.default_role` is `none`; roles by group from the ID token's `groups`; the dev sign-in's two locks; the principal's roles change on the next request after an assignment changes.

title: Build curation of metrics: edit, rename, merge, dismiss, verify, approve, history
content:
Read `docs/build/README.md` first (`ServiceContext`, `ServiceError`, book changes and events). Spec: `docs/specs/2026-10-25-powerbi-metrics-book.md`, sections The metrics book ("Metrics and variants", "Trust states", "Conventions", "Data model"), The connector and the API (the Curation and Review rows, the merge paragraph), The CLI (Metrics, Drafts, Variants rows), Extending it (events).

Services only; REST, MCP and CLI adapters come later and call these. Every function takes a `ServiceContext`, checks access first (`ctx.access.require(principal, { kind: "book", ... }, action)`), works in one transaction, and writes a `book_change` and an event.

Build `apps/api/src/services/book/`:

1. `metrics.ts`:
   - `getMetric(ctx, nameOrAliasOrId)`: the metric with the fields `get_metric` returns (spec's tool table): its base variant in each dataset the principal may describe (with `measure_reference`, the measure name in brackets), the other variants counted by shift, its category path, terms, failing checks (`checkMetric`), custom fields. A metric whose variants are all in datasets the principal may not describe, and which has variants, is `not_found`.
   - `listMetrics(ctx, filters & { cursor, limit })` with the spec's deterministic filters (`category` with or without children, `trust_state`, `unit`, `dataset`, `workspace`, `app`, `origin`, `name_prefix`, `custom.<key>`), keyset pagination.
   - `createMetric(ctx, input)`, `updateMetric(ctx, name, patch)` (any field the conventions allow, custom fields validated with `validateCustomFields`), `renameMetric(ctx, name, newName)`, `mergeMetrics(ctx, { from, into })` (moves every variant, deletes `from`; refused when units differ), `dismissMetric(ctx, name, reason)`, `deleteMetric(ctx, name)` (refused while it has variants).
   - Trust: a change by a token (`via` not `browser`) to an `agent_verified` metric sets `draft`; to a `human_verified` one sets `agent_verified` when every check still passes, else `draft`. `verifyMetric(ctx, name)` sets `agent_verified` when every check the conventions turn on passes, else answers `invalid` listing the failures. `approveMetric(ctx, name)` sets `human_verified`: refused unless `via` is `browser` or the conventions say `trust.human_verify_from: any` (this rule is code, with `approval_browser_only_security_test.ts`), and unless the checks pass. Any change sets `touched_at` if null and `origin` stays.
   - `metricHistory(ctx, name)`: its `book_change` rows.
Variants and the next drafts are issue curation_variants, which builds on this one.

Tests against real Postgres with the sample mirror (`apps/api/test/sample-mirror.ts`; principals' `powerbi_workspace_ids`, `powerbi_app_ids` and `powerbi_dataset_ids` built by hand from the sample tenant's access lists, since turning access lists into attributes is the visibility issue's) and the drafter run on it: each function's success and its refusal for a viewer; the trust transitions table (token edit of each state, approve from browser and from token, verify with a failing check); merge refused across units (a unit against none is refused too: set the draft's unit first); a viewer who may describe no dataset of a metric gets `not_found`.

content:
Read `docs/build/README.md` first ("image", "bootstrap environment", `AppDeps`). Spec: `docs/specs/2026-10-25-powerbi-metrics-book.md`, sections Architecture ("The units", migrations at start), Setup and the admin section (identities on first start), Security ("Containers"). Adapt Metrics Book's `apps/api/src/main.ts` and `apps/api/Dockerfile` (`../metrics-book/apps/api/`, read only).

Build:

1. `apps/api/src/deps.ts`: `buildDeps(config: Config): Promise<AppDeps>`: the pools for the container's role and `audit_writer`, the settings store, the identity (`loadIdentity`) and the secret reader, the guarded fetcher (`allowedOrigins` read from the settings `powerbi.authority`, `powerbi.api_url`, `powerbi.graph_url` and the embedding provider's base URL), access (`createAccess`), the clock, the logger.
2. `apps/api/src/main.ts`: the `api` command: `loadConfig(process.env, "api")`, migrations as the migrator (Metrics Book's `migrateDatabase`), `buildDeps`, `createApp`, serve on `PORT`, and a job runner for `runner = 'api'` jobs, all stopped cleanly on SIGTERM.
3. `apps/api/src/worker.ts`: the `worker` command: `buildDeps`, the job runner for `runner = 'worker'`, the schedule (`powerbi.sync.schedule` enqueues an incremental `sync`, `powerbi.sync.full_scan_schedule` a full one, `expire_results` every 15 minutes once that job exists), and one `sync` job enqueued with trigger `deploy` on start. A job name with no handler registered stays queued and is logged once, never failed, so the worker runs before the sync issue lands. Stops cleanly on SIGTERM.
4. `apps/api/src/services/jobs/all.ts` (a shared file, see the build README): both entries import it, so every job a later issue registers there runs in the right container. The sync issue may land before or after this one; whichever lands second keeps the other's line.

6. `apps/api/Dockerfile` (and `.dockerignore`): multi-stage, pnpm with the lockfile, build the api, a runtime stage on a pinned Node 24 slim image by digest, `ENV NODE_ENV=production`, `src/db/sql` copied beside `dist` (the migrations read it), the default Cerbos policies at `/app/access/policies`, the non-root user uid `10001` (all from the build README's "the image's runtime"), `IDENTITY_DIR` owned by that user, `ENTRYPOINT ["node", "dist/cli-entry.js"]` (or an equivalent) taking `api`, `worker` or `server ...`; `GIT_SHA` as a build argument. The web and docs builds are added by their issues later (leave a stage for them only when they exist; nothing empty now).
7. `apps/api/package.json` scripts `dev` (`tsx watch src/main.ts`), `start`.

Tests: `deps.test.ts` builds deps against the test database with the mock's URLs in settings; `worker.test.ts` starts the worker loop with a signal, sees the deploy `sync` job enqueued, a job registered by the test itself (`registerJob`) taken and finished, and the loop stop on the signal; the image builds (`docker build -f apps/api/Dockerfile .`) and `docker run --rm <image> server --help` exits 0.
