title: Build OAuth for MCP clients and the CLI's device flow, and bearer-token principals
content:
Read `docs/build/README.md` first. Spec: `docs/specs/2026-10-25-powerbi-metrics-book.md`, sections Access ("Sign-in and tokens": MCP clients, the CLI), Security (tokens, the checklist, the security tests list: token audience and expiry, refresh-token reuse, CIMD fetches to private addresses), The connector (what the consent screen states). Metrics Book's spec section "Sign-in and tokens (Better Auth)" holds the same design, word for word where it applies (`../metrics-book/docs/specs/2026-10-25-open-data-stack.md`). Read Better Auth 1.7.12's OAuth provider and MCP plugin docs, and the device authorization plugin's.

Build in `apps/api/src/services/auth/`:

1. `oauth.ts`: Better Auth's OAuth provider with its MCP support, configured as the spec says: Client ID Metadata Documents on (fetched only through `deps.fetcher.fetchUntrusted`), dynamic client registration as the fallback granting nothing until a person presses Allow, PKCE S256 only, `resource` required and bound into `aud` (`<PUBLIC_BASE_URL>/api/mcp`, or `/api/v1` for the CLI), RFC 9207 `iss`, one-hour JWT access tokens, rotating refresh tokens whose reuse revokes the grant (Better Auth issue #11317 is open: write that test first; if it fails, wrap the refresh endpoint so reuse revokes, and say so in your report), `client_id_metadata_document_supported: true` and `none` among `token_endpoint_auth_methods_supported` in the metadata.
2. The consent step as an API the SPA renders: `GET /api/v1/oauth/consent/{request}` (the person, the client's name, its redirect host, who made the client and when it was registered, what it will and will not be able to do) and `POST` Allow or Deny. The screen itself is the web issue's.
3. `device.ts`: the device authorization flow (RFC 8628) for `pbmb login`, as the build README's "The CLI's OAuth client" fixes it: the api registers the public client `pbmb-cli` at start (device_code and refresh_token grants only, resource `/api/v1`); the device authorization endpoint, advertised as `device_authorization_endpoint` in `/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server`; the user code confirmation as an API the SPA's `/device` page calls; the device grant served at the OAuth provider's own token endpoint, answering an access token and a refresh token with the same rotation and reuse detection as the MCP grants (if Better Auth's device plugin can only answer a session token, implement the grant on the provider's token endpoint instead, and say so in your report).
4. `/api/mcp`'s RFC 9728 metadata at `/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/api/mcp` (and for `/api/v1`), the authorization server metadata, and a 401 with `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer resource_metadata=...` from `/api/mcp` and `/api/v1` when no credential is sent; 403 with `insufficient_scope` when the token's scope does not cover the route.
5. `principal.ts`: the `authenticate` middleware accepts a bearer access token (signature, `iss`, `aud` for the path's resource, expiry), building a person principal with `via: "mcp"` or `"cli"` and `client_id` through sign-in's `personPrincipal(deps, person, { via, client_id })`, never a second builder; roles resolved per request as for sessions, including the person's stored sign-in groups (namespaced by provider, ignored once the sign-in that read them is 7 days old).
6. `ORIGIN_CHECK_EXEMPT` gains the token and device endpoints only; public paths gain the metadata documents and the OAuth endpoints Better Auth needs public.
7. `GET /api/v1/me/grants` and `DELETE /api/v1/me/grants/{id}` (a person's MCP and CLI grants, revocable at once), and the admin's `revoke_connection` on any grant (service function only; the admin routes come later).

Security tests: a token for `/api/v1` refused at `/api/mcp` and the other way round; an expired token refused; refresh-token reuse revokes the grant; a CIMD URL resolving to a private address refused; a DCR client gets nothing until Allow; PKCE plain refused; the 401 carries `resource_metadata`. Use the mock only for the person's sign-in; the OAuth flow is ours end to end in the test (an MCP-like client written in the test).

title: Build service accounts and their API keys
content:
Read `docs/build/README.md` first. Spec: `docs/specs/2026-10-25-powerbi-metrics-book.md`, sections Access ("Sign-in and tokens": service accounts), Decisions (service-account queries), Security (the checklist rows on credentials; API keys at most 90 days), Extending it (a service account reads the change feed).

Build:

1. `apps/api/src/db/schema/service-accounts.ts`: `service_account(name text primary key check (name ~ '^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{1,39}$'), owner_email, roles text[], workspace_ids uuid[], app_ids uuid[], source_cidrs cidr[], max_key_age_days int check (max_key_age_days between 1 and 90), disabled_at, created_by, created_at)` and `service_account_key(id uuid, service_account, prefix text, digest bytea unique, created_by, created_at, expires_at check (expires_at <= created_at + interval '90 days'), last_used_at, revoked_at)`; grants `api_rw`.
2. `apps/api/src/services/auth/service-accounts.ts`: `createServiceAccount`, `updateServiceAccount`, `disableServiceAccount`, `deleteServiceAccount`, `listServiceAccounts`, `createKey(ctx, name, { expires_in_days })` returning the key once (`pbmb_sk_` plus 32 random bytes, base64url), storing only its SHA-256 digest and an 8-character prefix for display, `listKeys`, `revokeKey`. Each change writes an `audit_event`. Access: `admin:manage_service_accounts`.
3. `principal.ts`: the `authenticate` middleware accepts `Authorization: Bearer pbmb_sk_...` on `/api/v1` (never on `/api/mcp`): looks the digest up in constant time, refuses an expired, revoked or disabled one, or a request from outside `source_cidrs` (the client address the proxy forwards, trusted only from the address `TRUSTED_PROXY` names: sign-in already added `TRUSTED_PROXY` to the bootstrap config and resolves the client address from it; reuse that, never a second parser), updates `last_used_at` at most once a minute, and builds a `service_account` principal with its roles and `powerbi_workspace_ids`/`powerbi_app_ids` attributes from its grants, `via: "api"`.
4. A rate limit per service account on `/api/v1` (60 requests a minute by default; the counter in Postgres so replicas share it: `request_rate(key, window_start, count)` in `apps/api/src/db/schema/rate-limit.ts`, a helper `apps/api/src/services/rate-limit.ts` that the query service reuses. `rate_limit` is Better Auth's own table, which sign-in added for its endpoints; leave it to Better Auth).

Security tests: `api_key_expiry_security_test.ts` (an expired key refused; a key whose `expires_at` exceeds 90 days refused by the database), a revoked key refused on the next request, a disabled account's keys all refused, the database holds no key in clear (`select` every column and search for the key), an API key refused on `/api/mcp`, a request from outside `source_cidrs` refused.

title: Build the Power BI connection: connect, encrypted tokens, refresh, groups, rekey and keep-alive
content:
Read `docs/build/README.md` first. Spec: `docs/specs/2026-10-25-powerbi-metrics-book.md`, sections Power BI ("A person's Power BI connection" steps 1 to 6, "Workspaces and apps": the person's groups), Access ("Sign-in and tokens": Microsoft sign-in chains into the connection; the matching email rule), Setup and the admin section (tokens encrypted for the api with age; rotation), Architecture (`rekey_tokens` and `refresh_idle_connections` run in the api), Security (the checklist rows on tokens).

Consumes: `src/powerbi/identity.ts` (`authorizationUrl`, `redeemCode`, `refresh`), `src/powerbi/graph.ts` (`myGroupIds`), `src/services/secrets/age.ts` (`encryptFor`, `decryptWith`) and the api's identity, `person_identity`, `registerJob`.

Build `apps/api/src/services/connection/`:

1. `apps/api/src/db/schema/connection.ts`: `powerbi_connection` as the spec gives it; grants `api_rw` only (the worker never reads it).
2. `connect.ts`: `GET /api/v1/powerbi/connect` (a signed-in person; state single use for 10 minutes, bound to the session, kept in Postgres; PKCE S256; `login_hint`; scopes `openid offline_access https://analysis.windows.net/powerbi/api/Dataset.Read.All https://graph.microsoft.com/User.Read`) and `GET /api/v1/powerbi/callback`: state checked, the code redeemed, `tid` must equal `powerbi.tenant_id`; a person who signed in with Microsoft must connect the same `oid`; anyone else's account must have their verified email when `powerbi.connection_requires_matching_email` is on; one Microsoft account connects to one person; then the tokens are encrypted for the api's recipient and stored, the person's groups read (`refresh` for Graph, then `myGroupIds`) into `person_identity`, and the browser sent back to where it came from (an allowlisted relative path only). The Microsoft sign-in chains here through its `callbackURL`: the web sign-in screen starts Microsoft's sign-in with `callbackURL` set to `/api/v1/powerbi/connect?next=<where the person was going>`, so `connect` must accept that arrival from a fresh session (and pass `next` through its allowlist). Do not change `services/auth/better-auth.ts`; the MCP OAuth issue is changing it at the same time. Test the chain by starting the mock sign-in with that `callbackURL`.
3. `tokens.ts`: `personPowerBiToken(ctx, { force_refresh }?)`: the person's access token, refreshed under `select ... for update` when it expires within five minutes or when `force_refresh` is set (the query service forces one refresh after Power BI answers 401), the new refresh token replacing the old in the same transaction; `needs_connection` errors with the sentence "Connect Power BI at <PUBLIC_BASE_URL>/settings/connections" when there is no connection, and "Your Power BI connection expired. Reconnect at ..." after `invalid_grant` (status `needs_reconnect`); updates `last_used_at`. Never logs or returns a token.
4. `groups.ts`: refresh the person's groups when `groups_read_at` is older than a day, on use.
5. `disconnect.ts`: `DELETE /api/v1/powerbi/connection` deletes both tokens and sets `disconnected`.
6. `jobs.ts`: `rekey_tokens` (runner `api`): every connection whose `recipient` is not the api's current one is decrypted with the retired identity still on disk and encrypted for the current one; extend `rotateIdentity` (`services/secrets/rotate.ts`) to enqueue it. `refresh_idle_connections` (runner `api`, daily when `powerbi.keep_connections_alive_days` is set): refreshes connections unused for that many days. Add both to `services/jobs/all.ts`.
7. `GET /api/v1/me` reports the connection's state and the link to connect (edit `routes/v1/me.ts`).

Security tests: no column of `powerbi_connection` holds a token in clear; the worker's identity cannot decrypt a token; a callback with another tenant's `tid` refused; a Microsoft-signed-in person connecting another `oid` refused; a second person connecting an `oid` already connected refused; a reused state refused; a redirect target outside the allowlist refused. Behaviour tests against the mock: connect end to end; refresh under concurrency (two queries at once spend one refresh token); revoked person turns `needs_reconnect`; groups read through Graph with paging; rekey after rotation; keep-alive refreshes an idle connection.

title: Build visibility: Power BI's access lists and a person's groups into the principal
content:
Read `docs/build/README.md` first (`Principal` attributes `powerbi_workspace_ids`, `powerbi_app_ids`, `powerbi_dataset_ids`). Spec: `docs/specs/2026-10-25-powerbi-metrics-book.md`, sections Power BI ("Workspaces and apps" in full), Access ("Decisions (Cerbos)": the three visibility modes), Security (the checklist row "People see only the metadata Power BI lets them reach").

Build `apps/api/src/services/access/visibility.ts`:

1. `powerbiAttributes(db, principal)`: for a person, from `person_identity` (their Microsoft object id and group ids) and `powerbi_access`: the workspaces listing them or one of their groups (any access right), the apps whose audience lists them or one of their groups, and the datasets shared with them directly; for a service account, its own `workspace_ids` and `app_ids`. One query, indexed; no per-row loops.
2. The `authenticate` middleware (`services/auth/principal.ts`) adds these attributes and `metadata_visibility` (from settings) to every principal it builds, once per request.
Take the person's Microsoft object id and Entra groups the way roles take them (`services/auth/roles.ts`: `roleSubject`, `readIdentity`), so the same freshness holds: groups read more than 7 days ago (`SIGN_IN_FRESH_MS`) give no workspace or app. One reader of a person's identity, never a second. `principal.ts` builds attributes in one place (`principalAttributes`); fill them there, for persons (sessions and bearer tokens alike) and service accounts.
3. A person with no Power BI connection and no `person_identity` gets empty lists: under `powerbi` they see no dataset, and `/api/v1/me` tells them to connect.

Tests against real Postgres after a real sync from the mock with the sample tenant (use the sync service, not hand-written rows, inside one rolled-back transaction after `takeSampleTurn`, as `services/sync/sync.test.ts` does: never commit the sample tenant): for every person in `EXPECTED_VISIBILITY` the describable datasets (`access.describableDatasets`) equal the expectation under `powerbi`; all datasets under `everyone`; none under `policy` with the default policies; the app-only viewer's dataset comes through the app; the analyst's comes through the group; the outsider sees nothing. Also tie the mock to the expectations: every person in `EXPECTED_QUERY_ACCESS` gets the answer it says from the mock's `executeQueries` on the org path and on the `groups/` path, with tokens from the mock's identity routes. `search_visibility_security_test.ts` comes with search; here `metadata_visibility_security_test.ts` asserts the outsider's `listDatasets` and `getMetric` answer like missing ones.

title: Build the first-run setup: the setup link and each step's check
content:
Read `docs/build/README.md` first. Spec: `docs/specs/2026-10-25-powerbi-metrics-book.md`, sections Setup and the admin section ("The first run": the link, the ten steps and their checks, the failures each check names), Power BI ("Two identities, two app registrations", tenant settings), Security ("Least privilege at Microsoft", the checklist).

Services and the setup API; the screens come later.

1. `apps/api/src/services/setup/link.ts`: with no admin (by the admin services' own rule, `hasAdmin(db)` in `services/admin/people.ts`: a `person` assignment of role `admin`; a group or domain admin may reach nobody who can sign in), the api logs a setup link at start (`<PUBLIC_BASE_URL>/setup?token=...`, a random token, its SHA-256 kept, 24 hours, single use: using it opens a setup session that lasts until the first admin exists) and `server setup-link` prints a new one (add the subcommand to `src/server.ts`). Once an admin exists, every setup route answers 404. `setup_link_security_test.ts`: a used token refused, an expired one refused, all refused once an admin exists.
2. `apps/api/src/services/setup/steps.ts`: the ten steps of the spec's table, each `{ id, title, fields, docs_path, check }`, and `GET /setup` (state: steps, which passed, what each needs) and `POST /setup/steps/{step}` (save the step's settings and secrets, run its check, return the result with the sentence and the one thing to change). Register each check with the admin's check registry so `/admin` re-runs them.
Each check answers a fixed sentence per known failure, never upstream text, through the admin services' `storeCheck` (`services/admin/checks.ts`), which caps a message at 300 characters and refuses one holding any piece of the value it checked; pass the value where the check holds it. A check of a worker-only secret runs in the worker, which holds the value, and stores its result there the same way.
3. The checks, each against the mock in tests, with every failure the spec names as its own sentence:
   - `address`: `PUBLIC_BASE_URL` is https (http only in development and test) and this request came in on it.
   - `app_registration`: client credentials for the app registration succeed at the token endpoint; after the admin signs in through Microsoft (the setup step's "Sign in now" goes through the normal sign-in, then back to `/setup`), the admin becomes the first admin, their connection is made, and their token's `scp` holds `Dataset.Read.All` and no write permission (any `ReadWrite` or `Tenant.` scope refuses the step with the sentence the spec's "Least privilege" bullet implies).
   - `scanner`: enqueues a `check` job with `runner = 'worker'` (the api cannot read the scanner's secret) which gets a token, calls `workspaces/modified`, scans one workspace, and stores the outcome; the api answers the step when the job finishes. Failures: the principal not allowed to call admin APIs; tables without columns and measures (detailed metadata off); measures without expressions (DAX setting off); a wrong secret.
   - `what_to_sync`: the workspaces found, for the screen to pick from; the first scan's size.
   - `sign_in`: each added provider's discovery or test sign-in.
   - `who_gets_in`: the list of people and groups the assignments would let in.
   - `search`: one sentence embedded through the configured provider (the embedder exists later; until then the step says search is off and passes with `provider: none`).
   - `agents`: the MCP address, the CLI install line; passes when the admin's own client has called `whoami` through the connector (until the connector exists, passes on the address being reachable).
   - `first_sync`: enqueues a full sync and reports its progress from `sync_run`, then the counts of measures and drafts.
   - `security`: the checklist items the stack can check live (https, cookies secure, the scanner's secret readable by the worker only, no write permission on the app registration, secrets with expiry dates, the identity volumes not world-readable), each passing or explained.
4. `setup.completed_steps` and `setup.completed_at` settings updated as steps pass.

Tests: the app registration's permission check (refusing `Tenant.Read.All`, `Tenant.ReadWrite.All` and any `ReadWrite` Power BI permission, each with its sentence) in `apps/api/src/services/setup/app-registration-check.test.ts` (the spec's security checklist names it); the whole setup through the API from an empty database against the mock, step by step, ending with an admin, a connection and a finished first sync; each check's failures through the mock's switches (`settings.service_principals_admin_apis`, `detailed_metadata`, `dax_expressions`, a wrong secret, a token with `Dataset.ReadWrite.All`).

title: Add the REST routes for curation, queries, threads, review and conventions
content:
Read `docs/build/README.md` first. Spec: `docs/specs/2026-10-25-powerbi-metrics-book.md`, section The connector (MCP) and the API: the REST table's Queries, Threads, Curation, Review and Conventions rows, the merge paragraph; Queries and results (the CSV route works with a signed link or the caller's own credential).

Thin adapters with `hono-openapi`'s `describeRoute` and zod validators, as the read routes are; answers snake_case JSON; errors through `error-response.ts`.

Build, each registered in `routes/v1/index.ts`:

- `routes/v1/curation.ts`: `GET /drafts/next`, `POST /metrics`, `PATCH /metrics/{name}`, `POST /metrics/{name}/merge`, `POST /metrics/{name}/verify`, `POST /metrics/{name}/dismiss`, `DELETE /metrics/{name}`, `GET /metrics/{name}/checks`, `GET /metrics/{name}/history`, `PATCH /variants/{id}`, `POST`/`PATCH`/`DELETE /categories/{path}`, `POST`/`PATCH`/`DELETE /terms/{name}`, `PUT`/`DELETE /terms/{name}/columns/{column_id}`, `PUT /elements/{kind}/{id}/docs`.
- `routes/v1/review.ts`: `POST /metrics/{name}/approve`: a session cookie only (the principal's `via` is `browser`); the service enforces it again.
- `routes/v1/conventions.ts`: `PUT /conventions`, `GET /conventions/versions`, `POST /conventions/diff`.
- `routes/v1/queries.ts`: `POST /queries`, `GET /queries`, `GET /queries/{id}`, `GET /results/{id}` (`offset`, `limit`), `POST /results/{id}/csv-link`, `GET /results/{id}/csv` (a valid `expires` and `signature` pair, or the caller's own credential; the signed form is a public path, so add it to the public-paths list with its test: the signature is the credential); each CSV download writes an `audit_event`. The CSV route sets `Content-Disposition: attachment` and `Cache-Control: no-store`; takes the owner from `verifyCsvLink`, never from the URL, and still reads through `resultCsv` so the store's owner check runs; the signed form gets a per-address rate limit (it is a public path); a request carrying both a credential and a link is judged by the link, and the link must name the same owner as the credential, else `not_found`.
- `routes/v1/threads.ts`: `POST /threads`, `GET /threads`, `GET /threads/{id}`, `POST /threads/{id}/replies`, `PUT` and `DELETE /threads/{id}/upvote`, `POST /threads/{id}/accept`, `POST /threads/{id}/archive`.

Tests: a curator's agent curating a draft end to end through REST (rename, describe, categorise, merge, move a variant with a shift, verify), a viewer refused on each write, approve refused with a bearer token and accepted with a session cookie, the CSV downloaded by signed link without a credential and refused with a tampered signature, a thread asked, answered and accepted.

title: Build running DAX: the query service, the result store and the query log
content:
Read `docs/build/README.md` first. Spec: `docs/specs/2026-10-25-powerbi-metrics-book.md`, sections Queries and results ("Running DAX" steps 1 to 7, "What the caller gets", "The result store" with `ResultStore`, "The query log"), Decisions (service-account queries), Security (results bound to their owner; the checklist rows on queries and results).

Consumes: `src/powerbi/execute.ts` (`executeQuery`), `src/powerbi/identity.ts` (`appServicePrincipalToken`), `src/services/connection/tokens.ts` (`personPowerBiToken`), `src/services/rate-limit.ts`, `src/dax/index.ts` (`referencedMeasures`), the `audit_writer` connection (`deps.auditDb`).

Build `apps/api/src/services/queries/`:

1. Schema `apps/api/src/db/schema/queries.ts`: `query_result`, `query_result_page`, `query_log` as the spec gives them (CHECK on `status`; `search_tsv` kept by a trigger in `apps/api/src/db/sql/queries.sql` over the DAX, the purpose and the dataset name; GIN index). Grants: `api_rw` select, insert, delete on the result tables; `worker_rw` select and delete on them (expiry); `audit_writer` insert on `query_log`; `api_rw` and `worker_rw` select on `query_log`.
2. `execute.ts`: `executeDax(ctx, { dataset, dax, purpose, preview_rows })` doing the spec's steps in order (and this rule for a stale token: when `executeQuery` throws `needs_connection` with `detail.status` 401, call `personPowerBiToken(ctx, { force_refresh: true })` once and retry; a second 401 answers `not_found`, like a dataset the person cannot reach; a refresh answering `invalid_grant` surfaces as `needs_connection`, the connection marked `needs_reconnect`; a 403 or 404 from Power BI is `not_found`; test each against the mock): `dataset:query` decided (a dataset the principal may not describe is `not_found`); the DAX checked (not empty, at most 100 KB, starting after comments with `EVALUATE` or `DEFINE`); the rate limit (`queries.rate_per_minute`); the row budget (`results.daily_row_budget` over the principal's `query_log` rows of the last 24 hours, refused with the time it frees up); the token (a person's delegated token; a service account's only when `powerbi.service_account_queries` is on, else `refused` with a sentence); `executeQuery`; the result saved through the store; the query logged once whatever the outcome (`succeeded`, `truncated`, `failed`, `refused`) with `measure_names` and their `metric_ids`; the anchor returned as the spec's JSON shows (`preview` capped at 100 rows and 16 KiB, saying so when it stops early; `csv_url` from the links module).
Cerbos's `result_owner` derived role compares the owner's kind as well as the id (service accounts issue): every result resource you build passes `owner_id` and `owner_kind`.
3. `store.ts`: `ResultStore` (the spec's interface) on Postgres: pages of 500 rows; `read(principal, id, range)` refuses any principal but the owner with `not_found`, caps `limit` at `results.page_rows_max` and 16 KiB; `stream` yields rows page by page; an expired result answers `not_found` with when it expired and its `query_id`; `deleteExpired(now)`.
4. `links.ts`: `csvLink(deps, result)` (HMAC-SHA256 over the result id, the owner and an expiry 15 minutes ahead, keyed by `result_link_key`, generated on first use), `verifyCsvLink(deps, id, expires, signature)` in constant time.
5. `csv.ts`: RFC 4180 CSV, UTF-8, a header row, streamed from the store.
6. `log.ts`: `searchQueryLog(ctx, { text, dataset, workspace, metric, principal, mine, status, since, until, cursor, limit })` (`query_log:read`; full text on `search_tsv` plus the filters; newest first; the DAX cut at 2,000 characters with `get_query` for the rest), `getQuery(ctx, id)`.
7. `expire.ts`: the `expire_results` job (runner `worker`, every 15 minutes from the worker's schedule: `worker.ts` already schedules it once a module registers it, behind `handlerFor("expire_results")`; make that entry unconditional), and its import in `services/jobs/all.ts`. The same job also calls `deleteOldEvents(db, now)` from `services/events/feed.ts` (the change feed keeps 90 days; `worker_rw` holds `delete` on `event` for this), with a test.

Security tests: `result_ownership_security_test.ts` (another person, a curator and an admin all get `not_found` for someone else's result, by id and by CSV with a valid signature for the owner); `query_identity_security_test.ts` (a person's query runs with that person's token: the mock records the token's `oid`); a CSV link with a changed id, owner or expiry refused; an expired link refused. Behaviour tests against the mock and the sample tenant: the anchor's shape; a truncated result; a DAX error passed on as Power BI's sentence; the row budget refusing; page two; CSV rows equal the pages; expiry deletes and then answers with the `query_id`; log search by a word of the DAX and by metric.

title: Build search: hybrid ranking, deterministic filters and the describe filter in one query
content:
Read `docs/build/README.md` first. Spec: `docs/specs/2026-10-25-powerbi-metrics-book.md`, sections Search ("Ranking", "Deterministic filters"), The connector (the `search` tool's input and answer), Security (the checklist row on search visibility). Metrics Book's spec describes the same hybrid search; the planner's search query (`../enumstudio-metrics-book/src/lib/`, find it with `grep -rl "rank" src/lib | head`) is the one both port; read it, write ours.

Build `apps/api/src/services/search/query.ts`: `search(ctx, { query, kinds, workspace, app, dataset, category, trust_states, unit, custom, include_removed, limit })` returning the spec's anchors and `search_mode`:

1. Exact matches first: a key, name or alias equal to the query (case-insensitive).
2. Then reciprocal rank fusion (k 60, pool 30 from each side) of pgvector cosine order over `embedding` (the query embedded by the api through the same embedder, `purpose: "query"`, compared only with vectors of the same `embedding_model`) and Postgres full text over `search_tsv` (`websearch_to_tsquery`).
3. The describe filter in the same SQL query, so a page is never thinned after the fact. `ctx.access.describableDatasets(principal)` is a condition over `powerbi_dataset`: join each document's `dataset_ids` to `powerbi_dataset` and apply it there, so the live plan (its row-level-security, endorsement and sensitivity attributes, and removals) decides rather than the arrays copied at embed time. A metric document is also filtered with `visibleMetric` (`services/mirror/read.ts`) on its `element_id`, the rule every other read of a metric uses. Documents with no dataset (terms without columns, categories) are visible to everyone signed in.
4. The deterministic filters as `where` clauses; `custom.<key>` against the `custom` jsonb.
5. With `search.provider: none`, words only, and `search_mode: "words_only"` with a sentence saying so.
6. `summary` cut at 240 characters; `limit` 10 by default, 50 at most.

Tests with the mock's embedding fakes and the sample tenant synced and drafted: an alias finds its metric first; a word in a description finds it by words; a filter by app returns only that app's datasets' elements; `search_visibility_security_test.ts`: the outsider gets no hit from any dataset, and a page of `limit` hits for a person is full when enough visible hits exist (no thinning); words-only mode says so.

title: Build the admin services: settings and secrets with checks, people and roles, status, export and import
content:
Read `docs/build/README.md` first. Spec: `docs/specs/2026-10-25-powerbi-metrics-book.md`, sections Setup and the admin section ("Settings and secrets", the settings and secrets tables, expiry warnings, `/admin` pages), A deployment (`book.yml`, `pbmb admin export|import`), Access ("Roles"), Security (the checklist).

Services only (`apps/api/src/services/admin/`), each taking a `ServiceContext`, checking the `admin` resource's action, writing an `audit_event` for every change. Routes come later.

1. `settings.ts`: `listSettings(ctx)` (every key, value, source, description), `setSetting(ctx, key, value, { save_failing })`: validates, runs the key's check when it has one (the setup issue registers checks; until then none), and saves only a passing value unless `save_failing`.
2. `secrets.ts`: `listSecrets(ctx)` (name, readers, set, hint, who, when, expiry, check status; never a value), `setSecret(ctx, name, value, { expires_at })` through `SecretWriter`, then its check when one is registered.
3. `checks.ts`: a registry, `registerCheck(stepOrKey, run)`, `runCheck(ctx, name)` storing `check_status` and `check_message` on the secret or in a `setting_check(key, status, message, checked_at)` table (`apps/api/src/db/schema/admin.ts`), and a daily `check` job (runner `api`; a check that needs the worker enqueues its own worker job) that re-runs every registered check. Add the job's module to `services/jobs/all.ts`.
A service account never holds `admin` and is refused every `admin:*` action in code (service accounts issue). If `pbmb admin status` must work under a read-only service account (the spec's deployment check), give status its own action (`admin:read_status`) that a non-admin role may hold, never `admin:*`.
4. `people.ts`: `listPeople(ctx)` (each person: email, sign-in method, effective roles and where each comes from, Power BI connection state, last seen), `listRoleAssignments`, `assignRole`, `revokeRole` (refusing to remove the last admin; a role name must be one the Cerbos policies define, and `access.default_role` likewise, or `none`; a group assignment names its provider: `microsoft` for Entra groups, or a provider id from `sign_in.providers`, as sign-in's `role_assignment.provider` column requires).
5. `status.ts`: `adminStatus(ctx)`: the last sync (from `sync_run`), checks failing, secrets expiring within 30 days, connections needing reconnect, the version and git sha. `pbmb admin status` and the admin page read this; `/api/v1/me` for an admin includes a short warning when a secret expires within 30 days.
6. `export.ts`: `exportBook(ctx)` returns `book.yml` (format 1: settings with a database source, the conventions, role assignments, service accounts without keys; never a secret), `importBook(ctx, yaml, { apply })` validates against `apps/api/src/services/admin/book.schema.json` (also shipped for the CLI), returns the difference, and applies it in one transaction when `apply` is true.

Tests against real Postgres, with the expiry warnings (30 and 7 days, in `adminStatus` and in an admin's `/api/v1/me`) in `apps/api/src/services/admin/secret-expiry.test.ts` (the spec's security checklist names it): each function and its refusal for a curator; the last admin cannot be removed; a secret's value never appears in any answer of this module (search every returned JSON for the value); export then import on an empty database gives the same export; a setting that fails its check is refused unless `save_failing`.

title: Port the MCP layer and mount the connector with its server instructions
content:
Read `docs/build/README.md` first. Spec: `docs/specs/2026-10-25-powerbi-metrics-book.md`, sections Decisions ("MCP layer"), The connector (MCP) and the API (the rules above the tool table), The metrics book ("Conventions": the server's instructions carry the guide's first paragraph), Access (MCP clients and protocol versions as Metrics Book's: 2026-07-28 and 2025-11-25 besides today's list).

Port the planner's JSON-RPC layer, as Metrics Book does: `../enumstudio-metrics-book/src/lib/mcp/{protocol,server,result,auth}.ts` and their tests `server.test.ts`, `surface.test.ts`, `scoping.test.ts` (read only; Enum Studio's own code). Keep its bounds: one POST, one message or a batch of at most 20, 1 MiB, errors never reaching the client beyond a sentence.

Build `apps/api/src/mcp/`:

1. `protocol.ts`, `result.ts`: as the planner's.
2. `server.ts`: `initialize` (protocol version negotiation; `serverInfo`; `instructions`: two short paragraphs saying what this connector is, to search before writing DAX, to keep results out of context, and the conventions' guide's first paragraph with "call get_conventions for the rest"), `tools/list`, `tools/call` dispatching to a registry, `ping`; notifications accepted and ignored.
3. `registry.ts`: `defineTool({ name, description, input: zod schema, handler: (ctx: ServiceContext, input) => Promise<unknown> })`; the input validated with zod and refused as `invalid` with the path of the problem; the answer serialised as snake_case JSON text, cut at 16 KiB with a sentence saying how to get the rest; a `ServiceError` answered as a tool error carrying its message.
4. Mount `POST /api/mcp` in `app.ts`, behind the bearer-token principal (`via: "mcp"`); no session; `GET` answers 405.
5. `tools/conventions.ts` with the first tool, `get_conventions` (calls `getConventionsForAgents`), and `tools/whoami.ts` (`whoami`: the principal, roles, the Power BI connection's state and the link to connect), so the layer is proved end to end. The other tools come in the next issues, one module per group in `tools/`, registered by importing `tools/index.ts` (create it with these two).
6. `connector_surface_security_test.ts`: lists every registered tool and fails when a tool's name is not on the spec's list of 27, or when a tool's handler reaches a book-changing service (assert on an allowlist of service modules each tool imports: no tool imports `services/book/{metrics,variants,categories,terms,docs}.ts` write functions or `services/conventions/store.ts`'s `setConventions`).

Tests: initialize, version negotiation, a batch of 21 refused, a body over 1 MiB refused, an unknown tool, an invalid input with its path, a tool error with its sentence, the 16 KiB cut; `whoami` through a real OAuth token from the auth issue's test helpers.

title: Build the embedders and the search documents, kept current by the embed job
content:
Read `docs/build/README.md` first. Spec: `docs/specs/2026-10-25-powerbi-metrics-book.md`, section Search ("What is embedded", "The embedder", the `search_document` and `embedding_usage` tables in the data model). Metrics Book's spec section "Search" describes the same design.

1. Schema `apps/api/src/db/schema/search.ts`: `search_document` and `embedding_usage` as the spec gives them (`embedding vector(1536)`, `cost_micro_usd bigint`; `search_tsv` maintained by a trigger in `apps/api/src/db/sql/search.sql`; GIN on `search_tsv`; an HNSW index on `embedding` with `vector_cosine_ops`, built with `maintenance_work_mem` kept small); grants: `worker_rw` all, `api_rw` select and insert on `embedding_usage`.
2. `apps/api/src/services/search/embedder.ts`: the spec's `Embedder` interface (put it here, not in `context.ts`), `createEmbedder(deps)` from `search.provider`, `search.model`, `search.base_url` (when it is empty, each provider's default host: import `EMBEDDING_HOSTS` from `apps/api/src/deps.ts`, which already gives the guarded fetcher those hosts, rather than repeating them) and the key (`openai_api_key` or `gemini_api_key` through `deps.secrets`), or null for `none`.
3. `openai.ts` and `gemini.ts`: plain HTTPS through `deps.fetcher.fetchFixed` (no SDK): OpenAI `POST /v1/embeddings` with `dimensions: 1536`, batches within 2,048 texts and 300,000 tokens; Gemini `batchEmbedContents` with `outputDimensionality: 1536` and a task prefix on each text by purpose (`task: search result | query: ...` for queries, `title: none | text: ...` for documents, as Google's guide for `gemini-embedding-2` says; cite the page you read). A 429 waits its `Retry-After` once. Every call recorded in `embedding_usage` with its cost in integer micro-dollars (OpenAI 0.13 and Gemini 0.20 dollars per million tokens, in a table in this module with the date read).
4. `documents.ts`: `buildDocuments(db, { element_ids? })`: one `search_document` per metric, variant, column and term (the spec's `search_text` for each), and per dataset, table, category with no embedding (words only); `dataset_ids`, `workspace_ids` and `app_ids` set for the describe filter; `custom` copied; removed and dismissed elements removed.
5. `embed-job.ts`: the `embed` job (runner `worker`): rebuild documents for changed elements, embed those whose `embedding_hash` (SHA-256 of provider, model and text) changed, in batches; with no provider, embeddings stay null. Add its import to `services/jobs/all.ts`. The sync already enqueues `embed`; curation changes enqueue it too (edit nothing in curation: record events, and have the job read the event feed since its last run to find changed elements).
6. Update the setup's `search` check (`services/setup/checks.ts`) to embed one sentence through the configured provider and report the cost of embedding the book as it stands.

Tests against the mock's embedding fakes: both providers' request shapes, batching, usage and cost recorded, a changed text re-embedded and an unchanged one not, a model change re-embedding everything, no provider leaving embeddings null, documents for each kind.

title: Read relationships and display folders with a person's token, on demand
content:
Read `docs/build/README.md` first. Spec: `docs/specs/2026-10-25-powerbi-metrics-book.md`, section Power BI ("Relationships and display folders" items 2 and 3).

Build `apps/api/src/services/mirror/info-views.ts`: `ensureModelDetails(ctx, datasetId)`, called by `getDataset` and `listMeasures` (edit `services/mirror/read.ts`): when the dataset's `relationships_source` is null, or `relationships_read_at` is older than its `schema_changed_at`, and the caller is a connected person, run `EVALUATE INFO.VIEW.RELATIONSHIPS()` and `EVALUATE INFO.VIEW.MEASURES()` through the query service (so both are logged under the person with the purpose "Read the dataset's relationships for the catalog", and the rate limit and budget apply), store the relationships (`relationships_source = 'info_view'`) and the measures' display folders, and set `relationships_read_at`. When Power BI refuses (no Build right, or `INFO` functions refused), set `relationships_source = 'unavailable'` and the time, and answer with relationships unknown and the sentence saying how to ask for them; do not retry before the schema changes again. A service account or a person with no connection never triggers the read.

title: Build questions and comments on any element: threads, replies, upvotes, views, accepted answers
content:
Read `docs/build/README.md` first. Spec: `docs/specs/2026-10-25-powerbi-metrics-book.md`, sections Questions and feedback (all of it), Access (the `thread` resource's actions), The connector (the thread tools: `post_thread`, `reply_in_thread`, `get_thread`, `list_threads`, `accept_reply`, `set_upvote`; open questions counted on `get_*` answers), Extending it (`thread.created`, `thread.answered` events).

1. Schema `apps/api/src/db/schema/threads.ts`: `thread`, `thread_reply`, `thread_upvote`, `thread_view` as the spec gives them (CHECKs on `kind`, `element_kind`, `status`; a question must have a title, a comment must not: a CHECK; `search_tsv` by a trigger in `apps/api/src/db/sql/threads.sql`). Grants `api_rw`.
2. `apps/api/src/services/threads/threads.ts`: `postThread(ctx, { kind, element, title, body })` (the element must exist and be visible to the principal), `reply(ctx, thread, body)`, `getThread(ctx, id)` (marks it viewed), `listThreads(ctx, { element, kind, status, mine, text, cursor })` (with reply and upvote counts and the replies since the principal last viewed), `acceptReply(ctx, thread, reply)` (the asker or a curator; sets `answered`), `archiveThread(ctx, id)` (a curator), `setUpvote(ctx, thread, upvoted)` (questions only, once per principal), `openQuestionsFor(db, elements)` (counts and accepted answers, for the `get_*` services to include). Every write records an event. A thread on an element the principal may not describe is `not_found`. Bodies are stored as written and never rendered as HTML here.
3. Edit `services/book/metrics.ts` `getMetric`, `services/book/terms.ts` `getTerm` and `services/mirror/read.ts` `getDataset` to include `open_questions` and `accepted_answers` from `openQuestionsFor`.

Tests against real Postgres with the sample mirror: each function and refusal; "my questions" with unread replies after another person replies and zero after `getThread`; accept by the asker and by a curator, refused for another viewer; one upvote per principal; a thread on a dataset the outsider cannot describe is `not_found` for them; `get_metric` carries the open question count.


Cerbos's `thread_author` derived role compares the author's kind as well as the id (service accounts issue): every thread resource you build passes `author_id` and `author_kind`.

title: Build the sign-in, consent, device and connections screens
content:
Read `docs/build/README.md` first. Spec: `docs/specs/2026-10-25-powerbi-metrics-book.md`, sections Access ("Sign-in and tokens (Better Auth)": providers, MCP clients, the CLI's device flow), Power BI ("A person's Power BI connection": connect, reconnect, `needs_reconnect`), Security (the consent's will and will-not lists, the redirect host shown, the checklist items on consent), The look ("Screens in v1": the `/sign-in`, `/oauth/consent`, `/device` and `/settings/connections` rows and what Trello, GitHub, Midday and Exa contribute). Martin's design rules: `~/.claude/docs/design.md`. Interface text: `~/.claude/docs/writing.md`. The API: `apps/api/openapi.json` (`/oauth/consent/*`, the device confirmation, `/me/connection`, `/me/grants`).

References (take structure, copy nothing): Trello's authorization page https://mobbin.com/screens/14dc3849-7cdf-489c-bde7-c9b807ba8f9c (a will and a will-not list, the redirect URL under the buttons); GitHub's, seen through Lovable https://mobbin.com/screens/b9cff604-859b-4a77-8568-c47ac5269137 (the redirect host under Authorize, who made the client and when); Midday's developer settings https://mobbin.com/screens/f5652b30-e34c-45c1-8cba-62fc4deb1f4a (a table per kind of access with an empty state); Exa's API keys page https://mobbin.com/screens/555f8e13-0103-47dc-a0ab-ae3c9172a0e8 (separate tabs for two kinds of access).

`/device` asks the person to type the code the CLI showed, never prefilled from a link, and shows when and from which address the request started (the device confirmation API returns both), so a code someone else sent cannot be approved with one click. The consent screen shows the client's `client_id` host as the vouched fact and its name as what the client claims. Build the routes `apps/web/src/routes/{sign-in,oauth-consent,device,settings-connections}.tsx` and their components in `apps/web/src/access/`:

1. **`/sign-in`**: Microsoft's button starts the sign-in with `callbackURL` set to `/api/v1/powerbi/connect?next=<next>`, so a Microsoft sign-in chains into the person's Power BI connection (the connection issue's `connect` accepts that arrival). One card, one button per provider the company turned on (from the public sign-in configuration the API serves), passkeys when on, the dev sign-in only when the API says it is on. `?next=` returns the person to where they were after sign-in, and only to a path on this origin (an absolute or protocol-relative URL is ignored). A refused sign-in (no role, email not matching) says why in one sentence: the api redirects back to `/sign-in` with `error=not_assigned` and the sentence in `error_description`; show that sentence (as text, never as HTML).
2. **`/oauth/consent`**: the person signed in, the client's name, who registered it and when, its redirect host set apart and in IBM Plex Mono, what it will be able to do (read the book, search, run DAX as you, ask questions) and what it will not (change the book, see what you cannot see in Power BI, act after you revoke it), Allow and Deny. Deny returns `access_denied` to the client.
3. **`/device`**: the code from the CLI, typed or from `?user_code=`, set in IBM Plex Mono; it names the client ("the pbmb command line") and the same will and will-not lists; Allow or Deny; a done state saying to go back to the terminal.
4. **`/settings/connections`**: two tabs. Power BI: connected or not, as whom, last used, Connect, Reconnect (when `needs_reconnect`, with the reason), Disconnect. Agents and the CLI: every MCP and CLI grant of this person (client, when granted, last used), Revoke each, with an empty state that says how to connect an agent (the MCP address to copy and a link to the docs page).

Every state designed: loading, error, expired consent request, wrong device code, nothing connected.

title: Build the setup guide screen
content:
Read `docs/build/README.md` first. Spec: `docs/specs/2026-10-25-powerbi-metrics-book.md`, sections Setup and the admin section ("The first run": the step rail, the ten steps, their checks and failure sentences), The look ("Screens in v1": the `/setup` row and what Mixpanel's and Retool's references contribute). Martin's design rules: `~/.claude/docs/design.md`. Writing for interface text: `~/.claude/docs/writing.md` (a button says what happens: "Check the scanner", not "Continue").

References (look, take structure, copy nothing): Mixpanel's Setup Guide flow https://mobbin.com/flows/27c04f35-efcf-4144-8a28-09fd7fdd6fd2 (a rail of steps with ticks; a step that waits for data and says what it found) and Retool's "Configure" resource flow https://mobbin.com/flows/05e7d9d2-77e5-4d27-a628-0d0670c5e066 (a form in sections, credentials apart, a help panel beside the form with the guide and troubleshooting links). You cannot open Mobbin; the spec's sentences on what each contributes are what you build from.

Build `apps/web/src/routes/setup.tsx` and its components (`apps/web/src/setup/`), on the setup API under `/api/setup/` (its routes are in `apps/api/src/routes/setup.ts`):

1. The link carries its token in the fragment (`/setup#token=...`). The screen POSTs the token to the setup API, which opens the setup session and sets its cookie, then removes the fragment with `history.replaceState` so the token stays out of history. Without a valid one, a sentence saying how to get a link (`docker compose exec api server setup-link`).
2. The rail on the left: the ten steps, each with its state (to do, passed, failing), the current one marked by the accent and its text, not colour alone. On a phone the rail becomes a step count and a list you open.
3. The step in the middle: what to do and why in short sentences; every value to copy (redirect URIs, permission names, the security group's purpose) in IBM Plex Mono with a copy button that confirms; the fields (secrets in password fields, never echoed back after saving; the expiry date of each client secret); a button that saves and runs the check, named for what it checks.
4. The result under the button: passed, or the check's sentence and the one thing to change, with the docs page for the step. A step that waits on the worker (the scanner check, the first sync) shows progress, by POSTing the step again every few seconds, and what it found when done. The first sync's button POSTs `{ "start_sync": true }`; the polls POST nothing, so they start nothing, and a failed sync shows its sentence with a button that starts it again ("214 measures in 12 datasets, 131 drafts ready for your agent").
5. "Need help?" beside the form: the docs page for the step and "When a check fails".
6. Step 2's "Sign in with Microsoft now" goes through the real sign-in and comes back to the setup, which shows the signed-in person's name and email and asks them to confirm ("Make me the admin") before they become the first admin. Until the first admin exists only steps 1 and 2 can run; the rest show that they wait for the admin.
7. Every state designed: loading, empty, error, a check that fails, the whole setup done (where to go next: connect agents, open the admin).

Tests: Playwright on the dev stack started empty (`pnpm dev:reset` then up with the setup left unfinished: add a flag `--no-setup` to `scripts/dev-stack.mjs` for it): the whole setup through the screens against the mock, a failing scanner check (the mock's admin API switch off through its control route) showing its sentence, light and dark at 390 and 1440 pixels (`check:ui` picks the route up).

content:

Martin's design rules: `~/.claude/docs/design.md`. Interface text: `~/.claude/docs/writing.md`. The admin API: `apps/api/openapi.json` (`/admin/*`).

Reference (take structure, copy nothing): Retool's "Configure" resource form https://mobbin.com/flows/05e7d9d2-77e5-4d27-a628-0d0670c5e066: settings in sections (general values apart from credentials), the help beside the form rather than under it.

1. **Status** (`/admin`): the last sync (when, how long, counts, errors in words), failing checks (each linking to its page), secrets expiring within 30 days, connections needing reconnect, the version and git sha; "Run a sync now" and the recent runs.
2. **Power BI** (`/admin/powerbi`): the app registration (tenant id, client id, secret with its expiry), the scanner registration (client id, secret with its expiry), what to sync (workspaces to include and exclude, personal workspaces, the two schedules with the next run shown in words), service-account queries, matching email, keeping connections alive; the cloud endpoints (`powerbi.authority`, `.api_url`, `.graph_url`) under "Another cloud". Each section ends in its Check.
3. **Sign-in** (`/admin/sign-in`): the providers turned on, each with its client id, issuer and secret and the redirect URI to copy; add Google or an OpenID Connect provider; passkeys on or off; Microsoft cannot be turned off while it is the only provider an admin can use.
4. **Search** (`/admin/search`): provider (OpenAI, Gemini, none), model, the key; the check's sentence and its cost estimate.
5. **Results and limits** (`/admin/limits`): result lifetime, preview rows, page size, the daily row budget, queries per minute.
6. **Secrets** (`/admin/secrets`): every secret: who reads it, set or not, its last four characters, who set it and when, its expiry (marked at 30 and 7 days), its last check and sentence; "Set" opens a password field once and never shows the value again; "Check" runs its check.

On every settings page: saving runs the key's check first; when it fails, the check's sentence shows with "Save anyway", which saves it marked failing; a value set by the environment shows read-only with "set by the environment (`VARIABLE_NAME`)"; a failing check anywhere shows as a band on every admin page linking to it. Loading, empty, error and refused states for each page.

Tests: Playwright on the dev stack (`e2e/fixtures.ts`, `signInAs` the sample admin): each page renders with the sample tenant's values; changing preview rows saves; setting a secret shows only its last four characters and the page source never holds the value; turning the scanner's admin API access off (`PATCH /_mock/settings` on the mock) makes the scanner's Check fail with its sentence, and "Save anyway" marks it failing with the band on every admin page; the sample viewer gets the admins-only page. `check:ui` covers the routes at 390 and 1440 pixels, light and dark.

Each command's help says what it answers in one sentence and shows one example. title: Add CLI commands for queries, results, questions, events, admin, service accounts, init and check
content:
Read `docs/build/README.md` first. Spec: `docs/specs/2026-10-25-powerbi-metrics-book.md`, sections The CLI (the Queries, Questions, Events, Admin and Deployment rows; `pbmb dax run --csv` downloading in one command), A deployment (`pbmb init`, `pbmb check`, `book.yml`), Setup and the admin section (`pbmb admin secrets set` prompts, never takes a value on the command line, refuses without a terminal). The API's shapes: `apps/api/openapi.json`.

Build in `apps/cli/src/powerbi_metrics_book/commands/`:

1. `dax.py`: `run <dataset> (--file <path> | --query <dax>) [--purpose] [--preview N] [--csv <path>]`: prints the preview and the result id; with `--csv` asks for the CSV link and streams the download to the file, printing only the path and the row count.
2. `results.py`: `read <id> [--offset] [--limit]`, `csv <id> -o <path>`.
3. `queries.py`: `search [<words>] [--dataset] [--metric] [--mine] [--status] [--since]`, `show <id>`.
4. `questions.py`: `list [--mine] [--status] [--element kind:id]`, `show`, `ask <kind> <id> --title --body`, `comment <kind> <id> --body`, `reply <thread> --body`, `accept <thread> <reply>`, `archive <thread>`, `upvote <thread> [--remove]`.
5. `events.py`: `pbmb events [--after <id>] [--kinds] [--follow]` (`--follow` polls every 5 seconds and prints new events as they come, one JSON line each with `--json`).
6. `admin.py`: `status`, `settings get [<key>]`, `settings set <key> <value> [--save-failing]`, `secrets list`, `secrets set <name> [--expires YYYY-MM-DD]` (reads the value with `getpass`; refuses when stdin is not a terminal or a value is passed as an argument), `check <name>`, `roles list|assign <role> --person|--domain|--group <value>|revoke <id>`, `people`, `audit [--since]`, `export [-o book.yml]`, `import <file> [--yes]`; `sync.py`: `run [--full]`, `status`; `sa.py`: `create <name> --owner --role [--workspace] [--app] [--max-key-age-days]`, `list`, `disable`, `delete`, `keys create <name> [--expires-in-days]` (prints the key once, with a sentence that it will not be shown again), `keys list <name>`, `keys revoke <name> <key-id>`.
7. `init.py` (local, no API): `pbmb init <dir>` writes a deployment directory: `compose.yml` (copied from the package's bundled copy of `stack/compose.yml`, the image tag set to this CLI's version), `cerbos/config.yaml` and `postgres/init/` beside it (the compose file binds both, relative to itself), `.env` with every bootstrap value and random passwords and `AUTH_SECRET` (mode 0600), `.gitignore` (ignoring `.env`), `access/policies/` and `access/tests/` (empty, with a README line on what goes there), `AGENTS.md` (the managed block between `<!-- powerbi-metrics-book:begin -->` and `<!-- powerbi-metrics-book:end -->`: how this deployment is started, upgraded, checked, and where its settings live); refuses a non-empty directory. Bundle what it copies in `powerbi_metrics_book/assets/` with a sync script `apps/cli/scripts/sync_assets.py` and a `--check` mode (as Metrics Book's).
8. `check.py` (local): `pbmb check [<dir>]`: validates `book.yml` (when present) against the bundled `book.schema.json` and `.env` for every bootstrap name, then runs the deployment's Cerbos policy tests in the pinned Cerbos image through Docker (`docker run --rm -v ...:/policies ghcr.io/cerbos/cerbos:0.57.0 compile --tests /policies/tests /policies`), with the shipped default policies layered first.

Tests with `httpx.MockTransport` and `tmp_path`: each remote command's output and `--json`; `dax run --csv` writing the file from a streamed answer; `secrets set` refusing without a terminal and refusing a positional value; `init` writing a 0600 `.env` with no value repeated across runs and refusing a non-empty directory; `check` on a valid and an invalid `book.yml` (the Docker step behind a marker that the default run includes; it needs Docker, which this machine has).

title: Build the docs site: Starlight in the shared look, served at /docs, with generated reference pages
content:
Read `docs/build/README.md` first. Spec: `docs/specs/2026-10-25-powerbi-metrics-book.md`, sections Docs, skills and the open-source files ("The docs site": the parts and their pages), The look ("One token set for both products"), Architecture (the api serves the docs). Writing: `~/.claude/docs/writing.md` (point first, every command and value to copy, each page ends with the check that proves the step worked; no em or en dashes, no curly quotes).

Build `apps/docs/` and what serves it:

1. Astro 7 with Starlight, `base: "/docs"`, built static to `apps/docs/dist`. Scripts `dev`, `build` (runs `scripts/sync-repo-docs.mjs`, then `astro build`), `check` (`scripts/check.mjs`, which runs every `scripts/check-*.mjs` in turn, so a later issue adds a check by adding a file).
2. The shared look: Starlight's colour, font and radius variables mapped from `@enum-studio/tokens` (`tokens.css`, `fonts.css`) in `src/styles/theme.css`, light and dark following Starlight's theme switch; the mark and "Power BI Metrics Book" as the site title; the tile as the favicon. Nothing else of its own.
3. The sidebar in `astro.config.mjs` with one group per part, each autogenerated from its directory so content issues add pages without touching the config: `start/`, `set-up/`, `deploy/`, `use/`, `make-it-yours/`, `security/`, `reference/`. Page order by `sidebar.order` in front matter.
4. Each part's opening page (`<part>/index.md`): what the part covers and who it is for, in a few sentences, with the order to read it in. The Start part in full: what it is and who it is for; a drawing of the stack (an inline SVG in the shared look: api with the SPA, worker, Postgres, Cerbos, the mock or Microsoft, the embedding provider; who talks to whom); the quickstart (`pbmb init`, `docker compose up -d`, `docker compose logs api` for the setup link, then the setup).
5. Generated reference pages, committed, each with a check that fails when stale (`--check`, run by `pnpm --filter @powerbi-metrics-book/docs check`):

This is the curating agent's main tool, so every command's output is written for an agent: short, complete, and with `--json` a document the agent can act on.

1. `metrics.py`: `list` (the filters), `show` (everything `get_metric` answers, failing checks first), `create`, `update` (`--label`, `--definition`, `--aliases` comma-separated or `none`, `--when-to-use`, `--not-the-same-as` text or `none`, `--grain`, `--unit`, `--category`, `--owner`, `--custom key=value` repeatable), `rename`, `merge <from> --into <to>`, `dismiss --reason`, `delete`, `check [<name> | --all]` (exit 1 when a check fails, listing each failure's sentence), `verify`, `request-review` (prints the review page's link and says a person must open it), `history`.
2. `drafts.py`: `next [--dataset] [--limit 10]`: each draft with its variants, their DAX, the datasets, the closest metrics and the suggested merges, in the order the API gives.
3. `variants.py`: `show <id>`, `move <id> --to <metric> [--period] [--comparison] [--comparison-period] [--currency] [--axis key=value] [--note]`.
4. `categories.py`: `tree`, `create <path> [--name] [--description]`, `rename`, `move <path> --to <parent>`, `delete`.
5. `terms.py`: `list`, `show`, `create <name> --definition ...`, `update`, `link <term> <column_id>`, `unlink`, `relate <term> <metric>`, `delete`.
6. `conventions.py`: `show` (the guide, then the rules in words), `edit` (writes the current YAML to a temporary file, opens `$EDITOR`, validates through `POST /conventions/diff`, shows the difference, asks, then `PUT`; refuses without a terminal), `set <dotted.path> <value>`, `diff <file>`, `validate <file>`, `export`, `import <file>` (shows the difference, asks unless `--yes`), `presets`.

Tests with `httpx.MockTransport`: each command, `--json` shapes, `metrics check --all` exit code, `conventions edit` with a fake editor, `import` asking without `--yes`.

title: Build the SPA's shell: Vite, router, typed API client, the shared look, served by the api
content:
Read `docs/build/README.md` first. Spec: `docs/specs/2026-10-25-powerbi-metrics-book.md`, sections The look (both parts), Architecture (the SPA is served by the api, holds no data of its own), Security (CSP). Martin's design rules: `~/.claude/docs/design.md` (read it before the first component). The planner's header and shell, to rebuild in React: `../enumstudio-metrics-book/src/components/chrome/Header.astro` and `src/components/shell/shell.css` (read only). Metrics Book's TypeScript standard for the SPA: `docs/standards/typescript.md` ("The SPA").

Build `apps/web/`:

1. Vite 8 with React 19, Tailwind 4 through `@tailwindcss/vite`, the theme from `@enum-studio/tokens` (`theme.css`, `tokens.css`, `fonts.css`), the tile as the favicon. Scripts `dev`, `build`, `typecheck`, `test` (vitest), `test:e2e` (Playwright), `types` (`openapi-typescript ../api/openapi.json -o src/api/schema.d.ts`; commit the output).
2. `src/api/client.ts`: `openapi-fetch` typed from that file, same-origin, credentials included; every datum comes from `/api/v1` through TanStack Query.
3. TanStack Router with code-based routes (no router plugin, so no generated route tree that every screen would rewrite): `src/router.tsx` builds the tree from one module per screen in `src/routes/`, and each screen issue adds its module plus one import and one entry in `src/router.tsx` (a shared-append file, see the build README). This issue builds the router and the root route only: `/` sends a signed-in person to `/settings/connections` and anyone else to `/sign-in`. Each screen's route is added by the issue that builds that screen (`/setup`, `/admin/*`, `/sign-in`, `/oauth/consent`, `/device`, `/settings/connections`, `/review/metrics/$name`), so no route exists before its screen does.
4. The shell: the header (the mark at 17px and "Power BI Metrics Book" set as the brand file says, the signed-in person, a sign-out), the light and dark theme following the system with a toggle that sets `data-theme` and is kept per person (localStorage, wrapped so a refusal changes nothing), the "Sample data" band when `/api/v1/me` says `sample_data`, a focus ring, an error boundary that says what went wrong in one sentence, and the empty and loading states as components the screens reuse.
5. The api serves the built SPA: `apps/api/src/http/static.ts` serving `apps/web/dist` at `/` with an `index.html` fallback for the SPA's routes (never for `/api/*`, `/docs`, `/health`), long cache headers on hashed assets, and the CSP allowing exactly what the build needs (no inline script). Add the web build stage to `apps/api/Dockerfile`.
6. `check:ui` (`apps/web/scripts/check-ui.ts` with Playwright): screenshots every route the app has at 390 and 1440 pixels wide, in light and dark, against the dev stack (`pnpm dev:up`), into `apps/web/test-results/` (gitignored), failing on a console error or a horizontal scroll.

7. `e2e/fixtures.ts`, the Playwright fixtures every screen's tests use: the dev stack's base URL (`node scripts/dev-stack.mjs url`), and `signInAs(page, email)` through `POST /api/auth/dev/sign-in` (the sample tenant's people: the admin, a curator, a viewer), so a screen's tests never depend on the sign-in screen being built.

Tests: vitest for the theme toggle and the client's error handling; Playwright: the shell renders signed in on the dev stack, the theme toggle switches, the band shows on the mock.

title: Add the dev stack command: the whole stack on the mock tenant per checkout
content:
Read `docs/build/README.md` first. Spec: `docs/specs/2026-10-25-powerbi-metrics-book.md`, section Development workflow ("`pnpm dev:up` ... starts the whole stack in Docker ... Ports and the compose project name come from a hash of the checkout's path"). Adapt Metrics Book's `mb dev up` port and name scheme (`../metrics-book/apps/cli/src/metrics_book/dev/`, read only).

Build `scripts/dev-stack.mjs` at the repository root (Node, no dependencies beyond Node 24) and root scripts `dev:up`, `dev:down`, `dev:reset`, `dev:logs`:

1. `up`: derives the compose project name and ports (api 30000 to 39999, Postgres and the mock beside it) from a hash of the checkout's absolute path; writes `.env.local` (gitignored) with development bootstrap values the first time (random passwords and `AUTH_SECRET`); runs `docker compose -f stack/compose.yml -f stack/dev/compose.dev.yml --env-file .env.local -p <name> up -d --build --wait`; then, so a developer starts signed in rather than at an empty setup, finishes the setup against the mock through the setup API under `/api/setup/` (the setup link read from the api's log, its token in the fragment; the app and scanner registrations of the sample tenant; the sample admin signed in through the mock's Microsoft sign-in and confirmed, by the same marker, OAuth state and confirm step a person goes through, with no shortcut in the api), and prints the URL, the setup state and how to sign in as each sample person.
Running from `stack/` must work as it does from a deployment made by `pbmb init`: `stack/compose.yml` binds `./access/policies` (the deployment's own Cerbos policies, layered on the defaults the image ships at `/app/access/policies`) with `create_host_path: false`, so add `stack/access/policies/README.md` saying the folder is a deployment's own policies and is empty in the repository (Cerbos reads only `.yaml`, `.yml` and `.json`). The Power BI mock builds the sample tenant's app registration from `SAMPLE_PUBLIC_BASE_URL`, so its redirect URIs match this checkout's api port: set it on the `powerbi-mock` service in `stack/dev/compose.dev.yml` from the same `PUBLIC_BASE_URL` the api gets. Build the image before anything mounts it (Cerbos mounts the `powerbi-metrics-book` image's policies as an image volume).
2. `down` (stops, keeps volumes), `reset` (removes the project's volumes too), `logs [service]`.
3. Running on the mock, the api answers `GET /api/v1/me` with `sample_data: true`, which the SPA uses for its "Sample data" band: set it from whether `powerbi.authority` points at the mock's origin (add that to `routes/v1/me.ts`).

Tests: `scripts/dev-stack.test.mjs` (node's test runner): the name and ports are stable for one path and differ for two; the `.env.local` written once and never overwritten. Then the real thing, once: `pnpm dev:up` from a clean checkout ends with the api healthy and the first sync finished, and `pnpm dev:reset` cleans up.

title: Write the setup guide: one page per setup step, Entra and Power BI click by click, and "When a check fails"
content:
Read `docs/build/README.md` first. Spec: `docs/specs/2026-10-25-powerbi-metrics-book.md`, sections Setup and the admin section (the ten steps and their checks), Power BI ("Two identities, two app registrations", "The sync", "Workspaces and apps", "A person's Power BI connection"), Access ("Sign-in and tokens", "Roles"), Search ("The embedder"), Docs, skills and the open-source files ("The docs site": the Set up part). Writing: `~/.claude/docs/writing.md`.

This is the guide Martin asked to be first class: a Power BI admin who has never registered an app in Entra follows it, or has their agent follow it, and gets it right the first time. The product's setup screens (`apps/web/src/setup/`) and the setup checks (`apps/api/src/services/setup/`) hold the words: the guide uses the same step names, the same field labels, and quotes each check's failure sentences exactly, so a person reading the guide and a person in the product see one procedure.

Write in `apps/docs/src/content/docs/set-up/`, one page per step, in the product's order:

1. `address.md`: `PUBLIC_BASE_URL`, https, what a proxy in front must pass on.
2. `app-registration.md`: in the Microsoft Entra admin center, every click and every value: a new registration, single tenant, the two redirect URIs (from the setup screen), the delegated permissions (`openid`, `profile`, `email`, `offline_access`, Power BI `Dataset.Read.All`, Graph `User.Read`) and why each, what to leave alone (no application permissions, no `Tenant.ReadWrite.All` or any write permission: the check refuses them), granting admin consent, a client secret and writing down its expiry; where each value goes in the setup.
3. `scanner.md`: the second registration with no API permissions and its secret; the security group holding its service principal and why a group; in the Power BI admin portal, the tenant settings by their exact names as the spec lists them ("Service principals can access read-only admin APIs" for that group only, "Enhance admin APIs responses with detailed metadata", "Enhance admin APIs responses with DAX and mashup expressions"); how long the settings take to apply; and, only for service-account queries, "Service principals can call Fabric public APIs" for the app's service principal and adding it to each workspace those queries may reach. Microsoft renames these settings now and then: say so, and give the setting's purpose beside its name so a reader can find a renamed one.
4. `what-to-sync.md`, 5. `sign-in.md` (Microsoft kept; Google: the client in Google Cloud console and its redirect URI; any OpenID Connect provider with Okta, Auth0 and Keycloak as named examples; passkeys), 6. `who-gets-in.md` (the default role, assignments by person, domain or group, and the three ways metadata is shown: `powerbi`, `everyone`, `policy`, with which fits an organisation that shares through apps and which through workspaces), 7. `search.md` (OpenAI or Gemini, what is sent to them and what is not, the cost estimate), 8. `agents.md` (the MCP address in Claude Code, Codex and Cursor, `pbmb login`, the skills), 9. `first-sync.md`, 10. `security.md` (the checklist step, linking the Security part).
11. `when-a-check-fails.md`: every check's failure sentences, grouped by step, each with its cause and the one fix; generated from the checks' sentence table where the setup issue exposes one, or written to match it exactly, with a test (`apps/docs/scripts/check-setup-sentences.mjs`, run by the docs `check`) that every failure sentence in `apps/api/src/services/setup/` appears on this page.
12. Running DAX for people: the "Semantic Model Execute Queries REST API" tenant setting (on by default), and Build permission on each semantic model; for a company that shares through apps, Build is granted when the app is published to its audience, and removing someone from the audience does not take it back (the spec's Workspaces and apps). Say it once in `who-gets-in.md` and link it from the steps that need it.

Every page: what this step is for in one or two sentences, what you need before you start, the steps numbered, every value in a code span or block to copy, and the check that proves the step worked (the setup's Check, or a `pbmb admin status` line). No screenshots of Microsoft's portals (they change and we cannot take them from a real tenant here); name each blade and button exactly instead.

content:
Read `docs/build/README.md` first. Spec: `docs/specs/2026-10-25-powerbi-metrics-book.md`, sections Security ("Controls": containers, "images pinned by digest, signed with cosign and shipped with an SBOM on release"; the checklist's last row), A deployment (the image tag `pbmb init` writes), Development workflow (GitHub Actions runs only the merge gate and releases).

Write `.github/workflows/release.yml`, run on a pushed tag `v*` only:

1. Check the tag equals the CLI's version (`apps/cli/pyproject.toml`) and `apps/api/src/version.ts`; stop otherwise.
2. Build the image from `apps/api/Dockerfile` for `linux/amd64` and `linux/arm64` with Buildx, push to `ghcr.io/enum-studio/powerbi-metrics-book:<version>`, with provenance and an SBOM attestation.
3. Sign the image by digest with cosign, keyless (GitHub's OIDC token), and attest the SBOM.
4. Build the CLI with `uv build` and publish it to PyPI through trusted publishing (no token stored).
5. Create the GitHub release with the compose file whose `api` and `worker` images are pinned to the pushed digest, and the verification command (`cosign verify` against the digest with the workflow's certificate identity and `https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com` as the issuer).

Every action pinned by full commit SHA with its version in a comment; least `permissions` per job (`contents: write` only for the release job, `packages: write` and `id-token: write` only where needed); `persist-credentials: false` on checkout; a concurrency group; timeouts. Write `docs/decisions/release.md`: why keyless signing, why GHCR and PyPI, and what Martin must set up before the first release (the PyPI trusted publisher, the package's visibility on GHCR once the repository is public).

The sandbox may refuse a command line containing `.github`; run such steps from a script file in your worktree. Lint the workflow with actionlint and zizmor, each from its pinned Docker image (`rhysd/actionlint:1.7.7`, `ghcr.io/zizmorcore/zizmor:1.11.0` with `--offline`), mounting the worktree read-only.

title: Add pnpm check:all: every test, every check, the scanners and the end-to-end test in one command
content:
Read `docs/build/README.md` first. Spec: `docs/specs/2026-10-25-powerbi-metrics-book.md`, sections Development workflow ("Test tiers": tier 3), Security ("Checks that run and security tests": the scanners and the semgrep rules), How it is tested. Metrics Book's full check is the model (`../metrics-book`, read only; find it with `grep -n check:all package.json` there and follow the script it names).

Build `scripts/check-all.mjs` and the root script `check:all`, which runs each step below in order, prints each step's name, result and duration as it goes, keeps going after a failure, and ends with a table of every step and exits 1 if any failed:

1. Formatting, lint, types: `pnpm fmt:check`, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm typecheck`, `uv run ruff format --check`, `uv run ruff check`, `uv run mypy apps/cli/src`.
2. Builds: api, web, docs, mock, the image (`docker build -f apps/api/Dockerfile .`).
3. Tests: api (vitest, real Postgres and Cerbos), mock, tokens, web (vitest), CLI (pytest), the Cerbos policy tests (`access/run_policy_tests.sh`, through the pinned Cerbos image), every `scripts/*.test.mjs` (`node --test`), and a check that every `FROM` in every Dockerfile is pinned by digest.
4. Generated files in step: the migration check (as the merge gate's), `openapi.json`, the CLI's bundled assets (`sync_assets.py --check`), the Codex skills (`sync-agent-skills.mjs --check`), the docs' reference pages and the docs `check`, `scripts/check-readme-links.mjs` when present, `deploy/check.sh`.
5. Scanners, each from its pinned image or pinned tool version, failing on any finding not in its allowlist file (each allowed finding with a reason and a date to look again): gitleaks over the history; osv-scanner over both lockfiles; trivy over the built image, the filesystem and `stack/compose.yml`; semgrep with the repository's rules in `.semgrep/rules/` (extend `no_fetch_outside_guarded_fetcher.yml` so it also refuses any `undici` import or call outside `apps/api/src/http/fetcher.ts`, with a test case) plus the new rule `no_route_without_credential_check.yml` (a Hono route registered outside the public-paths list without the authenticate middleware; with its test file, as the existing rules have); zizmor over `.github/workflows/`.
6. The UI: `check:ui` (screenshots of every route at 390 and 1440 pixels, light and dark, no console error, no horizontal scroll) on the dev stack.
7. The end-to-end test: `pnpm --filter @powerbi-metrics-book/api test:e2e`.

Then run it once on the integration branch as it stands and fix what it finds that belongs to the scanners' setup (allowlists with reasons, the new semgrep rule's findings). A failure in another issue's code is reported, not fixed here: list each with its step and first lines of output.
